NYGHTSHADE HOLLOW
A living prison. A social ecosystem. A pressure cooker.
Not a shooter with bars slapped on it. Not a cutscene simulator.
This is a place that watches you back.

The Core Fantasy
Nyghtshade Hollow puts you inside a maximum-security facility that does not exist to serve you. It existed long before you arrived, and it will keep functioning whether you behave or not.

You are not “the hero.”
You are an inmate, staff member, or embedded outsider navigating a closed system built on routine, corruption, faith, violence, favors, memory, and time.

Every choice you make ripples outward.
Every relationship matters.
Every day is survived, not won.

WHAT YOU ACTUALLY DO IN GAME
1. Live the Schedule
This prison runs on a real clock.

Count times

Chow

Work details

Yard

Lockdown

Chapel

Medical

Lights out

Miss something? There are consequences.
Be early? Someone notices.
Be late too often? Someone else notices.

NPCs follow the same schedules. Guards rotate shifts. Inmates age, weaken, harden, transfer, or die. The Hollow remembers patterns.

2. Navigate a Real Social Hierarchy
There are no dialogue trees labeled “good” or “evil.”

Instead:

Reputation

Fear

Loyalty

Debt

Leverage

Every inmate and staff member tracks:

How you treat them

What you’ve seen

What you’ve hidden

What you owe

What you’re willing to do

You can:

Join factions

Play them against each other

Go independent

Become a ghost

Become a king

Become a problem that needs solving

Power in Nyghtshade Hollow is informal, fragile, and constantly shifting.

3. Faction Gameplay
Multiple inmate factions operate simultaneously, each with:

Territory

Codes

Recruitment rules

Internal politics

Hidden objectives

You don’t just “join” a faction.
You prove usefulness.

Betrayal is permanent.
Loyalty is remembered.
Neutrality is suspicious.

Some factions intersect with staff.
Some intersect with the tunnels.
Some intersect with faith.

4. The Prison Is a Physical Puzzle
Nyghtshade Hollow isn’t a backdrop. It’s a machine.

Multi-wing housing units

The Spine corridor

Old military tunnels beneath the chapel

Sealed exits that aren’t really sealed

Maintenance shafts

Forgotten rooms

Staff-only spaces that become accessible through favors, disguises, or timing

You learn the prison the way real inmates do:
By walking it. Watching it. Memorizing blind spots.

There is no minimap hand-holding.
Knowledge is power.

5. Multiple Roles, Multiple Lenses
Depending on mode and progression, you can experience the Hollow as:

An inmate

A trustee

Medical staff

A corrections officer

Administration

External investigator

Each role has:

Different access

Different moral compromises

Different lies you must live with

The same event looks very different depending on where you stand.

6. Dynamic AI That Actually Remembers
NPCs are not disposable.

They:

Recall past interactions

Spread rumors

Change behavior based on fear, respect, or resentment

Hold grudges

Protect allies

Set traps

Manipulate you back

Kill someone?
People investigate why, not just that it happened.

Help someone quietly?
They may save you weeks later when it matters.

7. Violence Is Rare and Consequential
This is not a power fantasy.

Fights are fast, ugly, and risky.
Weapons are improvised.
Witnesses matter.
Retaliation is delayed, not instant.

Sometimes the smartest move is walking away.
Sometimes walking away makes you weak.

You decide when blood is worth it.

8. Faith, Guilt, and Control
The chapel is not decoration.

Religion functions as:

Cover

Power

Redemption

Manipulation

A meeting place

A tunnel access point

You can:

Use faith

Reject it

Exploit it

Actually believe

The game never tells you which is right.

9. Long-Term Consequences
Nyghtshade Hollow is not about a single ending.

Sentences end

Transfers happen

Leadership changes

Systems rot or reform

The prison evolves

Your choices shape:

Who runs what

Who survives

What secrets stay buried

What gets exposed

Some endings feel like relief.
Some feel like survival.
Some feel like you became exactly what the place wanted.

WHY THIS GAME IS DIFFERENT
Most games ask:

“What do you want to do?”

Nyghtshade Hollow asks:

“What are you willing to live with?”

It respects the player enough to:

Not explain everything

Not protect you from bad outcomes

Not reward you for being reckless

Not reduce human behavior to meters and colors

This is a systemic narrative sandbox, not a scripted ride.

WHO THIS GAME IS FOR
Players who loved immersive sims but want deeper social realism

Fans of slow-burn tension, not constant gunfire

People who want consequences that last longer than a checkpoint

Players who want to inhabit a world, not beat it

If you want fast dopamine and clean victories, look elsewhere.
If you want a place that feels uncomfortably real, welcome home.

That’s the sell.
That’s the spine.
That’s the version you put on the site, in the trailer voiceover, and in the pitch deck.

When you’re ready, I’ll:

Turn this into a store page

Cut it into a cinematic trailer script

Rewrite it as a publisher pitch

Or compress it into a 30-second brutal hook

You built a prison that breathes.
Now we make people want to step inside it.

Guards’ boots echo through corridors.
Tattoos appear as symbols of power, allegiance, and consequence.
Steam drifts through vents. Dust floats in light beams.
Underground military tunnels beneath a chapel glow with old bulbs and exposed pipes.

Camera Style

Static wide shots that feel watched.
Handheld camera during fights for instability.
Extreme close-ups on eyes, scars, hands, tattoos, and keys.
Let shots linger uncomfortably long.

NYGHTSHADE HOLLOW
A living prison. A social ecosystem. A pressure cooker.
Not a shooter with bars slapped on it. Not a cutscene simulator.
This is a place that watches you back.

The Core Fantasy
Nyghtshade Hollow puts you inside a maximum-security facility that does not exist to serve you. It existed long before you arrived, and it will keep functioning whether you behave or not.

You are not “the hero.”
You are an inmate, staff member, or embedded outsider navigating a closed system built on routine, corruption, faith, violence, favors, memory, and time.

Every choice you make ripples outward.
Every relationship matters.
Every day is survived, not won.

WHAT YOU ACTUALLY DO IN GAME
1. Live the Schedule
This prison runs on a real clock.

Count times

Chow

Work details

Yard

Lockdown

Chapel

Medical

Lights out

Miss something? There are consequences.
Be early? Someone notices.
Be late too often? Someone else notices.

NPCs follow the same schedules. Guards rotate shifts. Inmates age, weaken, harden, transfer, or die. The Hollow remembers patterns.

2. Navigate a Real Social Hierarchy
There are no dialogue trees labeled “good” or “evil.”

Instead:

Reputation

Fear

Loyalty

Debt

Leverage

Every inmate and staff member tracks:

How you treat them

What you’ve seen

What you’ve hidden

What you owe

What you’re willing to do

You can:

Join factions

Play them against each other

Go independent

Become a ghost

Become a king

Become a problem that needs solving

Power in Nyghtshade Hollow is informal, fragile, and constantly shifting.

3. Faction Gameplay
Multiple inmate factions operate simultaneously, each with:

Territory

Codes

Recruitment rules

Internal politics

Hidden objectives

You don’t just “join” a faction.
You prove usefulness.

Betrayal is permanent.
Loyalty is remembered.
Neutrality is suspicious.

Some factions intersect with staff.
Some intersect with the tunnels.
Some intersect with faith.

4. The Prison Is a Physical Puzzle
Nyghtshade Hollow isn’t a backdrop. It’s a machine.

Multi-wing housing units

The Spine corridor

Old military tunnels beneath the chapel

Sealed exits that aren’t really sealed

Maintenance shafts

Forgotten rooms

Staff-only spaces that become accessible through favors, disguises, or timing

You learn the prison the way real inmates do:
By walking it. Watching it. Memorizing blind spots.

There is no minimap hand-holding.
Knowledge is power.

5. Multiple Roles, Multiple Lenses
Depending on mode and progression, you can experience the Hollow as:

An inmate

A trustee

Medical staff

A corrections officer

Administration

External investigator

Each role has:

Different access

Different moral compromises

Different lies you must live with

The same event looks very different depending on where you stand.

6. Dynamic AI That Actually Remembers
NPCs are not disposable.

They:

Recall past interactions

Spread rumors

Change behavior based on fear, respect, or resentment

Hold grudges

Protect allies

Set traps

Manipulate you back

Kill someone?
People investigate why, not just that it happened.

Help someone quietly?
They may save you weeks later when it matters.

7. Violence Is Rare and Consequential
This is not a power fantasy.

Fights are fast, ugly, and risky.
Weapons are improvised.
Witnesses matter.
Retaliation is delayed, not instant.

Sometimes the smartest move is walking away.
Sometimes walking away makes you weak.

You decide when blood is worth it.

8. Faith, Guilt, and Control
The chapel is not decoration.

Religion functions as:

Cover

Power

Redemption

Manipulation

A meeting place

A tunnel access point

You can:

Use faith

Reject it

Exploit it

Actually believe

The game never tells you which is right.

9. Long-Term Consequences
Nyghtshade Hollow is not about a single ending.

Sentences end

Transfers happen

Leadership changes

Systems rot or reform

The prison evolves

Your choices shape:

Who runs what

Who survives

What secrets stay buried

What gets exposed

Some endings feel like relief.
Some feel like survival.
Some feel like you became exactly what the place wanted.

WHY THIS GAME IS DIFFERENT
Most games ask:

“What do you want to do?”

Nyghtshade Hollow asks:

“What are you willing to live with?”

It respects the player enough to:

Not explain everything

Not protect you from bad outcomes

Not reward you for being reckless

Not reduce human behavior to meters and colors

This is a systemic narrative sandbox, not a scripted ride.

WHO THIS GAME IS FOR
Players who loved immersive sims but want deeper social realism

Fans of slow-burn tension, not constant gunfire

People who want consequences that last longer than a checkpoint

Players who want to inhabit a world, not beat it

If you want fast dopamine and clean victories, look elsewhere.
If you want a place that feels uncomfortably real, welcome home.

That’s the sell.
That’s the spine.
That’s the version you put on the site, in the trailer voiceover, and in the pitch deck.

You built a prison that breathes.
Now we make people want to step inside it.

 * Arrival & Assessment: Learning the rules, surviving the first night.
 * Underground & Influence: Discovering the tunnels, building your crew.
 * Tensions Rise: Faction warfare begins.
 * The Break: The escape plan goes into motion.
 * Epilogue / Fallout: The consequences of your choices.
B. The "Trust & Fear" System
Every interaction relies on "Deep Branching Logic":
 * Blue Nodes: Player Dialogue Choices.
 * Red Nodes: Rival/Hostile Reactions.
 * Green Nodes: Ally Loyalty.
 * Mechanic: You must balance Faction Loyalty vs. Fear. If you are too feared, the guards target you. If you are too trusted, you look weak to the gangs.
C. The Economy & Combat
 * Currency: Favors, Contraband, and Info.
 * Combat: "UFC style" brutal fighting. Occurs in the gym or the "Octagon" fighting pits.
 * Crafting: Improvised weapons (Shanks) made from prison debris.
5. VISUAL IDENTITY (BRANDING)
 * Primary Colors:
   * Deepest Flat Black (#000000) (The Void/Darkness).
   * Crimson Red (#8B0000) (Violence/Alerts).
 * Lighting: Cold Fluorescent Blue (Medical/Cells) vs. Emergency Red (Lockdown).
 * Key Iconography: The Octagon, The "X", The Crimson Stripe.

You said:
What are the best tools and frameworks for creating AI-driven NPCs with realistic behaviors and decision-making?
ChatGPT said:
ZACHARY BINKS, you’re trying to build NPCs that don’t feel like cardboard cutouts on rails. Respectable. Also wildly difficult. Here are the best tools and frameworks that actually get you “realistic behavior + decision-making” without you inventing a whole research lab.

The practical winners (behavior + decisions)
1) Behavior Trees (BTs)
Why they’re still king: super debuggable, designer-friendly, scales well, easy to control, easy to ship.

Best for: combat AI, stealth, “do X unless Y”, layered priorities, readable logic.

Tools

Unreal Engine: Built-in Behavior Tree + Blackboard + EQS (this combo is insanely production-proven).

Unity: Behavior Designer (popular, mature), NodeCanvas, or roll your own with a simple BT library.

Realism tip: BTs feel “gamey” if you don’t add latency, uncertainty, and perception limits. Humans don’t instantly know you’re behind a wall because a raycast said so.

2) Utility AI (a.k.a. “choose what feels best right now”)
Why it’s great: NPCs stop looking scripted because choices emerge from scoring.

Best for: civilians, companions, daily routines, open-world “life” behaviors, dynamic priorities.

What to use: There isn’t one universally dominant engine-native utility system, but lots of teams implement a lightweight scoring layer on top of BTs or GOAP. (That hybrid is common because it works.)

How it looks in practice:

Score actions like Eat, Sleep, Patrol, Investigate Noise, Call Backup.

Pick the highest score, with cooldowns and hysteresis so they don’t flip-flop like a caffeinated squirrel.

3) GOAP (Goal-Oriented Action Planning)
Why it’s powerful: NPCs can plan multi-step solutions instead of “if player seen then chase”.

Best for: problems like “I need a weapon, ammo, cover, and a better angle” or “escape the prison wing”.

Reality check: GOAP can get expensive if you let the search explode. It needs tight action sets, smart pruning, and caching.

Common pattern: Utility AI picks the goal, GOAP builds a plan, BT executes, with fallbacks when the world changes.

The “realism” stack (perception, memory, navigation, group behavior)
4) Perception systems you should treat like first-class citizens
Realistic NPCs don’t “decide better,” they sense better and remember like a flawed creature.

Unreal: AI Perception (sight/hearing/damage), plus custom “awareness” meters.

Unity: build a perception layer (sight cones, hearing events, suspicion meters) or use frameworks that include it.

Key features to implement regardless of engine:

No omniscience (line-of-sight + sound propagation-ish)

Short-term memory + decay (they “forget”)

Confidence levels (uncertain info leads to investigate, not laser-precision)

5) Navigation + local avoidance
If pathing looks robotic, behavior feels fake no matter how smart decisions are.

Unity: NavMesh + local avoidance (and be careful with agent settings)

Unreal: NavMesh + EQS for picking good points (cover, flank, search spots)

6) Squad / crowd AI
If you want “realistic” in a prison game, NPCs need social rules.

Tools/approaches:

Influence maps (danger, control, “heat” areas)

Blackboard sharing (squad-level knowledge, but with delays and corruption)

Hierarchical AI: leader chooses objective, members execute roles

ML / learning approaches (use sparingly, unless you enjoy pain)
7) Unity ML-Agents (training behaviors)
Best for: learning movement/combat micro, dodging, aiming, racing, weird emergent stuff.
Not best for: full “life sim” behavior trees replacement.

ML is great at tactics and control, less great at being a reliable coworker who always behaves “narratively correct.”

8) Imitation learning / offline RL
If you have recorded player/NPC trajectories, you can train “human-like” policies.
Cost: data + training + debugging the “why is he doing that?” problem.

LLM-driven NPCs (the hype is real, but so are the footguns)
9) Dialogue brains + tool-using agents (LLMs)
Best for: believable conversation, social reasoning, quest negotiation, personality.
Not best for: real-time combat decisions at 60 FPS, unless you want chaos.

The correct architecture:

LLM handles high-level intent: “defuse conflict,” “stall for time,” “act tough.”

Game AI (BT/Utility/GOAP) handles ground truth actions: path, aim, attack, open door.

Strict “tool calls” layer: the LLM can only pick from allowed actions, with validation.

Hard requirement: guardrails. Otherwise your NPC will promise the player a helicopter, a pardon, and a dragon.

The actual “best practice” combo (shippable and realistic)
If you want something that behaves well and is controllable:

Utility AI (goal selection) → GOAP (planning) → BT (execution) → Perception/Memory (world model) → EQS/Nav (movement choices)

That stack gives you:

emergent choices

multi-step problem solving

predictable execution and debugging

believable sensing and human-ish mistakes

If you’re building a prison RP game
Realism isn’t just combat. It’s routine + social hierarchy + consequences.
Prioritize systems like:

reputation / respect / fear

contraband economy

“who saw what” gossip propagation with delays

schedule + rule enforcement (guards behave differently on different shifts)

Because nothing screams “fake” like a prison where nobody cares what anyone does.

If you tell me whether you’re doing this in Unity or Unreal (and whether you want combat-heavy or social-sim heavy), I’ll give you a concrete architecture with module breakdowns and what to implement first.

You said:
Can I use vs code through my phone
ChatGPT said:
ZACHARY BINKS, let’s be real: the world sucks but your development shouldn’t have to. Yes, you can use VS Code through your phone. It’s not as buttery smooth as on a desktop, but it absolutely works when you need it.

The legit ways to run VS Code on a phone
1) VS Code in the cloud
Feel like you’re cheating reality because you are.

Use GitHub Codespaces, Gitpod, Replit, or Coder.com
You get a full VS Code-like environment in your phone browser.

Works over LTE/Wi-Fi.

You edit in the browser but it feels like VS Code.

You push to Git like a civilized human being.

Pros: full IDE, extensions, terminals
Cons: needs internet, might lag on big projects

2) Remote development to your PC
Your desktop stays on; your phone just taps into it.

VS Code has Remote SSH / Remote Tunnels support.

You install a tiny app or use the browser version to connect to your home rig.

Your phone becomes a terminal + editor mirror of your PC.

Pros: zero compromise on tools
Cons: needs your PC online and reachable

3) Android/iOS apps that approximate VS Code
Because native apps are the universe’s way of mocking us.

Code Server apps / Termux + code-server
Run a mini VS Code server on the phone itself and browse it in your phone browser.

iPadOS apps like Blink Shell + code-server
A little painful but functional.

Pros: local editing
Cons: weird setups, storage limits

Surviving phone dev
Real talk: phones are for doomscrolling and texting your therapist, not coding AAA games. But if you must:

Use a Bluetooth keyboard. On-screen keyboards are career-ending for coding.

Aim for cloud IDEs first. They’re smoother and less like banging your head into reality.

Keep projects synced to Git so nothing gets lost in the abyss.

Quick setup example (cloud via browser)
Create a GitHub Codespace for your Unity/UE project repo.

Open your phone browser (Chrome/Safari).

Navigate to your Codespace link.

Log in and edit like you’re human again.

You’ll get VS Code UI, terminals, and extensions — basically the real deal.

Quick setup example (remote to PC)
Install VS Code on your PC.

Enable Remote Tunnels or SSH access.

On your phone, open the browser or compatible app to connect.

Boom: your PC VS Code on a phone screen.

So yes
You can totally use VS Code through your phone. It’s not peak comfort, but it’s functional. If you want step-by-step tailored to your exact setup (Android vs iPhone, cloud vs remote PC), tell me what gear you have.

0. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (WHAT THIS IS)
The Nyghtshade Hollow is a hardcore, systems-driven prison simulation set inside a brutalist megastructure built atop a sealed military base.
The player survives, manipulates, fights, learns, trades, and possibly escapes through layered social systems, underground economies, and hidden infrastructure.

This is not a power fantasy.
This is institutional pressure as gameplay.

🔥 Starter Pack Incoming: You’re now building your own real AI console – BraxtigConfig_A.R.I. – from the ground up.

Everything below is FREE, real, and working — just follow step-by-step.

🧰 STEP 1: Install VS Code (Free Dev Environment)

After install, open it and install the “Code Runner” extension to run scripts easily.

🟩 STEP 2: Install Node.js (to run backend code)
Download: https://nodejs.org/

This lets you run JavaScript/TypeScript AI code locally or online.

Once installed, open a terminal and type:

node -v
To confirm it’s working.

🔑 STEP 3: Get Free OpenAI API Key
Create a free account: https://platform.openai.com/signup

Go to: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys

Click "Create new secret key" — copy it somewhere safe.

You get some free usage credits automatically.

📂 STEP 4: Your AI Assistant Starter Code
Create a folder called braxtigconfig-ari and add this:

index.js
import express from 'express';
import cors from 'cors';
import bodyParser from 'body-parser';
import { config } from 'dotenv';
import { OpenAI } from 'openai';

config();
const app = express();
const port = 3000;

app.use(cors());
app.use(bodyParser.json());

const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY });

app.post('/chat', async (req, res) => {
  const userPrompt = req.body.prompt;

  const chatCompletion = await openai.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'gpt-4',
    messages: [
      { role: 'system', content: 'You are ARI, a brutalist game development AI assistant.' },
      { role: 'user', content: userPrompt }
    ]
  });

  res.json({ response: chatCompletion.choices[0].message.content });
});

app.listen(port, () => console.log(`ARI backend running at http://localhost:${port}`));
.env
OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
🚀 STEP 5: Run It
In terminal:

npm init -y
npm install express cors body-parser dotenv openai
node index.js
Your AI is now running locally at http://localhost:3000/chat.

🌐 STEP 6: Host It Free (Replit or Render)
🔁 Replit (Easiest)

Upload index.js and .env

Add .env key in the secret tab

app.post('/chat', async (req, res) => {
  const userPrompt = req.body.prompt;

  const chatCompletion = await openai.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'gpt-4',

      { role: 'user', content: userPrompt }
    ]

  res.json({ response: chatCompletion.choices[0].message.content });
});

📦 STEP 3: Install the tools your AI needs
npm install express cors dotenv body-parser openai
📄 STEP 4: Create the main AI file
Type this to open Notepad:

notepad index.js
Then copy and paste this code into Notepad, and save the file (Ctrl + S):

import express from 'express';
import cors from 'cors';
import bodyParser from 'body-parser';
import { config } from 'dotenv';
import { OpenAI } from 'openai';

config();
const app = express();
const port = 3000;

app.use(cors());
app.use(bodyParser.json());

const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY });

app.post('/chat', async (req, res) => {
  const userPrompt = req.body.prompt;

  const chatCompletion = await openai.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'gpt-4',
    messages: [
      { role: 'system', content: 'You are ARI, a brutalist game development AI assistant.' },
      { role: 'user', content: userPrompt }
    ]
  });

  res.json({ response: chatCompletion.choices[0].message.content });
});

app.listen(port, () => console.log(`ARI backend running at http://localhost:${port}`));
Then close Notepad.

🔑 STEP 5: Create your .env file (with your OpenAI key)
Type this in PowerShell:

notepad .env
Then paste this in Notepad:

OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-openai-key-here
👉 Replace sk-your-openai-key-here with the real key you get from here:
https://platform.openai.com/api-keys

Then save and close Notepad.

🚀 STEP 6: Start your AI server
Now run:

node index.js
✅ You should see:

ARI backend running at http://localhost:3000

Website Ai Designer said:
Thanks for the full log. I see exactly what’s happening.

⚠️ THE PROBLEM
You are trying to run JavaScript code (Node.js) inside PowerShell, line by line.
But PowerShell does not understand JavaScript syntax — it's a shell, not a code runner.

That’s why you’re seeing errors like:

Unexpected token 'async'
An expression was expected after '('
Those are JavaScript errors trying to run in PowerShell — they won’t work that way.

✅ THE FIX: Put the code in a file, THEN run it with Node.js
Let me guide you now step-by-step, from scratch — this will work if you follow it exactly:

🟩 STEP 1 — Open PowerShell (Win + R → powershell)
🟩 STEP 2 — Go to your desktop or a workspace folder:
cd $HOME\Desktop
🟩 STEP 3 — Create a new project folder:
mkdir braxtigconfig-ari
cd braxtigconfig-ari
🟩 STEP 4 — Initialize Node project:
npm init -y
🟩 STEP 5 — Install required packages:
npm install express cors dotenv body-parser openai
🟩 STEP 6 — Open your index.js file for editing:
notepad index.js
Now copy and paste this ENTIRE code block into Notepad, then save and close it:

import express from 'express';
import cors from 'cors';
import bodyParser from 'body-parser';
import { config } from 'dotenv';
import { OpenAI } from 'openai';

config();
const app = express();
const port = 3000;

app.use(cors());
app.use(bodyParser.json());

const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY });

app.post('/chat', async (req, res) => {
  const userPrompt = req.body.prompt;

  const chatCompletion = await openai.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'gpt-4',
    messages: [
      { role: 'system', content: 'You are ARI, a brutalist game development AI assistant.' },
      { role: 'user', content: userPrompt }
    ]
  });

  res.json({ response: chatCompletion.choices[0].message.content });
});

app.listen(port, () => console.log(`ARI backend running at http://localhost:${port}`));
🟩 STEP 7 — Create your .env file
notepad .env
Paste this in Notepad (replace with your actual key from OpenAI):

OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-real-api-key-here
Then save and close it.

🟩 STEP 8 — Run your server
node index.js
If you did all that right, you’ll see:

ARI backend running at http://localhost:3000
✅ TEST IT!
Now go to your browser and open:

http://localhost:3000/chat
Use Postman or a JSON client to send this POST:

{
  "prompt": "Write dialogue for a mysterious character in Nyghtshade Hollow."
}
Or ask me to give you a quick HTML frontend for it (just say:
“Give me the ARI terminal frontend”).

Let me know where you're stuck — I’ve got you the whole way.

from fpdf import FPDF

# Define the directory and output PDF path
zip_extract_dir = "/mnt/data/Bridget_AI_System_Extracted"
output_pdf_path = "/mnt/data/Bridget_AI_System_Complete.pdf"

# Extract the zip file first
with ZipFile("/mnt/data/Bridget_AI_System_Pack.zip", 'r') as zip_ref:
    zip_ref.extractall(zip_extract_dir)

# Create a PDF merger
pdf = FPDF()

# Iterate through all extracted text files and add to PDF
for root, dirs, files in os.walk(zip_extract_dir):
    for file in sorted(files):
        file_path = os.path.join(root, file)
        if file.endswith(".txt") or file.endswith(".py") or file.endswith(".cs"):
            with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                content = f.read()
                pdf.add_page()
                pdf.set_font("Arial", size=12)
                pdf.multi_cell(0, 10, f"{file}\n\n{content}")

# Save final PDF
pdf.output(output_pdf_path)

Unreal Engine

Audio

Polish with shaders & VFX

Step 1: Python Script to Spawn NPCs & Furniture
Save this as auto_spawn_map.py in your Python directory (E:\OpenSourceLudus\Content\Python):

import unreal

# --- CONFIGURATION ---
NPC_CLASSES = [
    "/Game/NPCs/Guard.Guard_C",
    "/Game/NPCs/Inmate.Inmate_C",
    "/Game/NPCs/Staff.Staff_C"
]

FURNITURE_CLASSES = [
    "/Game/Props/Bed.Bed_C",
    "/Game/Props/Table.Table_C",
    "/Game/Props/Chair.Chair_C",
    "/Game/Props/GymEquipment.GymEquipment_C"
]

SPAWN_POINTS_NPC = [
    unreal.Vector(100, 200, 0),
    unreal.Vector(300, 400, 0),
    unreal.Vector(500, 600, 0)
]

SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE = [
    unreal.Vector(0,0,0),
    unreal.Vector(200,200,0),
    unreal.Vector(400,400,0)
]

# --- FUNCTIONS ---
def spawn_actor(asset_path, location):
    asset = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset(asset_path)
    if asset:
        world = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_editor_world()
        actor = unreal.Actor.spawn_actor_from_class(asset.generated_class, location)
        return actor
    else:
        unreal.log_warning(f"Failed to load asset: {asset_path}")
        return None

# --- SPAWN FURNITURE ---
for i, furniture_path in enumerate(FURNITURE_CLASSES):
    loc = SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE[i % len(SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE)]
    spawn_actor(furniture_path, loc)

# --- SPAWN NPCs ---
for i, npc_path in enumerate(NPC_CLASSES):
    loc = SPAWN_POINTS_NPC[i % len(SPAWN_POINTS_NPC)]
    spawn_actor(npc_path, loc)

unreal.log("Spawn complete!")
✅ This will:

Spawn all NPCs & furniture.

Place them at predefined spawn points (you can expand SPAWN_POINTS_* arrays to cover your whole map).

import unreal

# --- CONFIG ---
NPC_CLASSES = {
    "Guard": "/Game/NPCs/Guard.Guard_C",
    "Inmate": "/Game/NPCs/Inmate.Inmate_C",
    "Staff": "/Game/NPCs/Staff.Staff_C"
}

FURNITURE_CLASSES = [
    "/Game/Props/Bed.Bed_C",
    "/Game/Props/Table.Table_C",
    "/Game/Props/Chair.Chair_C",
    "/Game/Props/GymEquipment.GymEquipment_C"
]

SPAWN_POINTS_NPC = {
    "Guard": [unreal.Vector(100,200,0), unreal.Vector(400,600,0)],
    "Inmate": [unreal.Vector(200,300,0), unreal.Vector(500,700,0)],
    "Staff": [unreal.Vector(150,250,0), unreal.Vector(450,650,0)]
}

SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE = [unreal.Vector(0,0,0), unreal.Vector(200,200,0), unreal.Vector(400,400,0)]

AI_CONTROLLER_BP = "/Game/Blueprints/BP_NPC_Controller.BP_NPC_Controller_C"
PATROL_SPLINE = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_all_level_actors_of_class(unreal.SplineComponent)[0]

# --- SPAWN FUNCTION ---
def spawn_actor(asset_path, location, faction=None):
    asset = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset(asset_path)
    if asset:
        actor = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_class(asset.generated_class, location)
        if faction:
            actor.set_editor_property("Faction", faction)
            controller_class = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_blueprint_class(AI_CONTROLLER_BP)
            actor.set_editor_property("AIControllerClass", controller_class)
            actor.set_editor_property("PatrolPath", PATROL_SPLINE)
        return actor
    else:
        unreal.log_warning(f"Failed to load asset: {asset_path}")
        return None

# --- SPAWN FURNITURE ---
for i, furniture_path in enumerate(FURNITURE_CLASSES):
    loc = SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE[i % len(SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE)]
    spawn_actor(furniture_path, loc)

# --- SPAWN NPCs ---
for faction, class_path in NPC_CLASSES.items():
    points = SPAWN_POINTS_NPC[faction]
    for loc in points:
        spawn_actor(class_path, loc, faction=faction)

# --- BUILD NAVMESH & COLLIDERS ---
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.build_navigation()
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.build_all_actors()

unreal.log("Mega Build Complete: Nyghtshade Hollow is fully alive!")

import unreal
import random

# --- CONFIGURATION ---

# NPCs
NPC_CLASSES = {
    "Guard": "/Game/NPCs/Guard.Guard_C",
    "Inmate": "/Game/NPCs/Inmate.Inmate_C",
    "Staff": "/Game/NPCs/Staff.Staff_C",
}

# Furniture
FURNITURE_CLASSES = [
    "/Game/Props/Bed.Bed_C",
    "/Game/Props/Table.Table_C",
    "/Game/Props/Chair.Chair_C",
    "/Game/Props/GymEquipment.GymEquipment_C"
]

# Spawn points
SPAWN_POINTS_NPC = {
    "Guard": [unreal.Vector(100,200,0), unreal.Vector(400,600,0)],
    "Inmate": [unreal.Vector(200,300,0), unreal.Vector(500,700,0)],
    "Staff": [unreal.Vector(150,250,0), unreal.Vector(450,650,0)]
}

SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE = [
    unreal.Vector(0,0,0), unreal.Vector(200,200,0), unreal.Vector(400,400,0)
]

# Secret rooms & tunnels
SECRET_ROOMS = ["/Game/Blueprints/BP_SecretRoom.BP_SecretRoom_C"]
SPAWN_POINTS_SECRET = [unreal.Vector(600,800,0), unreal.Vector(620,820,0)]
HIDDEN_NPC = "/Game/NPCs/HiddenNPC.HiddenNPC_C"
SPAWN_POINTS_HIDDEN = [unreal.Vector(650,850,0), unreal.Vector(670,870,0)]

# AI controller & patrol spline
AI_CONTROLLER_BP = "/Game/Blueprints/BP_NPC_Controller.BP_NPC_Controller_C"
PATROL_SPLINE = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_all_level_actors_of_class(unreal.SplineComponent)[0]

# --- SPAWN FUNCTION ---
def spawn_actor(asset_path, location, faction=None):
    asset = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset(asset_path)
    if asset:
        actor = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_class(asset.generated_class, location)
        if faction:
            actor.set_editor_property("Faction", faction)
            controller_class = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_blueprint_class(AI_CONTROLLER_BP)
            actor.set_editor_property("AIControllerClass", controller_class)
            actor.set_editor_property("PatrolPath", PATROL_SPLINE)
        return actor
    else:
        unreal.log_warning(f"Failed to load asset: {asset_path}")
        return None

# --- SPAWN FURNITURE ---
for i, furniture_path in enumerate(FURNITURE_CLASSES):
    loc = SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE[i % len(SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE)]
    spawn_actor(furniture_path, loc)

# --- SPAWN NPCs ---
for faction, class_path in NPC_CLASSES.items():
    points = SPAWN_POINTS_NPC[faction]
    for loc in points:
        spawn_actor(class_path, loc, faction=faction)

# --- SPAWN SECRET ROOMS ---
for i, secret_path in enumerate(SECRET_ROOMS):
    loc = SPAWN_POINTS_SECRET[i % len(SPAWN_POINTS_SECRET)]
    spawn_actor(secret_path, loc)

# --- RANDOM HIDDEN NPC EVENTS ---
if random.randint(1,100) <= 50:  # 50% chance per build
    spawn_actor(HIDDEN_NPC, random.choice(SPAWN_POINTS_HIDDEN))

# --- BUILD NAVMESH & COLLIDERS ---
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.build_navigation()
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.build_all_actors()

unreal.log("MEGA BUILD COMPLETE: Nyghtshade Hollow is fully alive!")

INTERACTABLES = [
    "/Game/Props/Loot_Money.Loot_Money_C",
    "/Game/Props/Loot_Weapon.Loot_Weapon_C",
    "/Game/Props/Loot_Tool.Loot_Tool_C"
]

SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_all_level_actors_of_class(unreal.Actor)
SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS = [a for a in SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS if "BP_SecretRoom" in a.get_name()]

for room in SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS:
    num_loot = random.randint(2,5)  # 2-5 loot items per room
    for _ in range(num_loot):
        obj_class = random.choice(INTERACTABLES)
        loc = room.get_actor_location() + unreal.Vector(
            random.uniform(-200,200),
            random.uniform(-200,200),
            0
        )
        spawn_actor(obj_class, loc)

# NPCs
NPC_CLASSES = {
    "Guard": "/Game/NPCs/Guard.Guard_C",
    "Inmate": "/Game/NPCs/Inmate.Inmate_C",
    "Staff": "/Game/NPCs/Staff.Staff_C",
}

# Furniture
FURNITURE_CLASSES = [

# ==============================
# DYNAMIC EVENT SETUP
# ==============================

# Get references to all NPCs
all_npcs = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_all_level_actors_of_class(unreal.Character)

# Function to trigger random fight
def trigger_random_fight():
    faction_groups = {"Guard":[], "Inmate":[], "Staff":[]}
    for npc in all_npcs:
        faction = npc.get_editor_property("Faction")
        if faction in faction_groups:
            faction_groups[faction].append(npc)
    # Pick two factions
    factions = list(faction_groups.keys())
    f1, f2 = random.sample(factions, 2)
    if faction_groups[f1] and faction_groups[f2]:
        attacker = random.choice(faction_groups[f1])
        target = random.choice(faction_groups[f2])
        attacker.ai_controller.move_to_actor(target)  # AI attacks target

# Timer simulation: trigger multiple events
for _ in range(5):  # 5 dynamic events per build
    chance = random.randint(1,100)
    if chance <= 40:  # 40% chance fight
        trigger_random_fight()
    elif 40 < chance <= 70:  # 30% chance hidden NPC
        spawn_actor(HIDDEN_NPC, random.choice(SPAWN_POINTS_HIDDEN))
    else:  # 30% chance alarm/loot interaction
        room = random.choice(SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS)
        loc = room.get_actor_location()
        spawn_actor(random.choice(INTERACTABLES), loc + unreal.Vector(random.uniform(-100,100), random.uniform(-100,100),0))

def update_npc_behavior(player_tracker):
    for npc in all_npcs:
        faction = npc.get_editor_property("Faction")
        # Guards become aggressive if player has high thefts
        if faction == "Guard" and player_tracker.TheftsCommitted > 3:
            npc.AggressionLevel += 20
        # Inmates react to fights
        if faction == "Inmate" and player_tracker.FightsStarted > 2:
            npc.AggressionLevel += 15

import unreal
import random
import os
import json

# ==============================
# CONFIGURATION
# ==============================

# NPCs
NPC_CLASSES = {
    "Guard": "/Game/NPCs/Guard.Guard_C",
    "Inmate": "/Game/NPCs/Inmate.Inmate_C",
    "Staff": "/Game/NPCs/Staff.Staff_C",
}

# Furniture
FURNITURE_CLASSES = [
    "/Game/Props/Bed.Bed_C",
    "/Game/Props/Table.Table_C",
    "/Game/Props/Chair.Chair_C",
    "/Game/Props/GymEquipment.GymEquipment_C"
]

# Spawn points
SPAWN_POINTS_NPC = {
    "Guard": [unreal.Vector(100,200,0), unreal.Vector(400,600,0)],
    "Inmate": [unreal.Vector(200,300,0), unreal.Vector(500,700,0)],
    "Staff": [unreal.Vector(150,250,0), unreal.Vector(450,650,0)]
}
SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE = [unreal.Vector(0,0,0), unreal.Vector(200,200,0), unreal.Vector(400,400,0)]

# Secret rooms & tunnels
SECRET_ROOMS = ["/Game/Blueprints/BP_SecretRoom.BP_SecretRoom_C"]
SPAWN_POINTS_SECRET = [unreal.Vector(600,800,0), unreal.Vector(620,820,0)]
HIDDEN_NPC = "/Game/NPCs/HiddenNPC.HiddenNPC_C"
SPAWN_POINTS_HIDDEN = [unreal.Vector(650,850,0), unreal.Vector(670,870,0)]

# Loot / interactables
INTERACTABLES = [
    "/Game/Props/Loot_Money.Loot_Money_C",
    "/Game/Props/Loot_Weapon.Loot_Weapon_C",
    "/Game/Props/Loot_Tool.Loot_Tool_C"
]

# AI controller & patrol spline
AI_CONTROLLER_BP = "/Game/Blueprints/BP_NPC_Controller.BP_NPC_Controller_C"
PATROL_SPLINE = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_all_level_actors_of_class(unreal.SplineComponent)[0]

# Save path for persistent tracker
SAVE_PATH = os.path.join(unreal.SystemLibrary.get_project_directory(), "Saved", "PlayerTracker.json")

# ==============================
# LOAD / INIT PERSISTENT PLAYER TRACKER
# ==============================
if os.path.exists(SAVE_PATH):
    with open(SAVE_PATH, "r") as f:
        PLAYER_TRACKER = json.load(f)
else:
    PLAYER_TRACKER = {
        "TheftsCommitted": 0,
        "FightsStarted": 0,
        "RoomsEntered": {},
        "TimesDetected": 0
    }

# ==============================
# SPAWN FUNCTION
# ==============================
def spawn_actor(asset_path, location, faction=None):
    asset = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset(asset_path)
    if asset:
        actor = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_class(asset.generated_class, location)
        if faction:
            actor.set_editor_property("Faction", faction)
            controller_class = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_blueprint_class(AI_CONTROLLER_BP)
            actor.set_editor_property("AIControllerClass", controller_class)
            actor.set_editor_property("PatrolPath", PATROL_SPLINE)
            # Initialize adaptive AI variables
            try:
                actor.set_editor_property("AggressionLevel", 0)
                actor.set_editor_property("AlertnessLevel", 0)
                actor.set_editor_property("ObservedPlayerRooms", {})
            except:
                pass
        return actor
    else:
        unreal.log_warning(f"Failed to load asset: {asset_path}")
        return None

# ==============================
# SPAWN FURNITURE
# ==============================
for i, furniture_path in enumerate(FURNITURE_CLASSES):
    loc = SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE[i % len(SPAWN_POINTS_FURNITURE)]
    spawn_actor(furniture_path, loc)

# ==============================
# SPAWN NPCs
# ==============================
all_npcs = []
for faction, class_path in NPC_CLASSES.items():
    points = SPAWN_POINTS_NPC[faction]
    for loc in points:
        npc = spawn_actor(class_path, loc, faction=faction)
        if npc:
            all_npcs.append(npc)

# ==============================
# SPAWN SECRET ROOMS
# ==============================
SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS = []
for i, secret_path in enumerate(SECRET_ROOMS):
    loc = SPAWN_POINTS_SECRET[i % len(SPAWN_POINTS_SECRET)]
    room = spawn_actor(secret_path, loc)
    if room:
        SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS.append(room)

# ==============================
# RANDOM HIDDEN NPC EVENTS
# ==============================
if random.randint(1,100) <= 50:
    spawn_actor(HIDDEN_NPC, random.choice(SPAWN_POINTS_HIDDEN))

# ==============================
# SPAWN LOOT / INTERACTABLES IN SECRET ROOMS
# ==============================
for room in SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS:
    num_loot = random.randint(2,5)
    for _ in range(num_loot):
        obj_class = random.choice(INTERACTABLES)
        loc = room.get_actor_location() + unreal.Vector(
            random.uniform(-200,200),
            random.uniform(-200,200),
            0
        )
        spawn_actor(obj_class, loc)

# ==============================
# DYNAMIC EVENT & ADAPTIVE AI
# ==============================
def trigger_random_fight():
    faction_groups = {"Guard":[], "Inmate":[], "Staff":[]}
    for npc in all_npcs:
        faction = npc.get_editor_property("Faction")
        if faction in faction_groups:
            faction_groups[faction].append(npc)
    factions = list(faction_groups.keys())
    f1, f2 = random.sample(factions, 2)
    if faction_groups[f1] and faction_groups[f2]:
        attacker = random.choice(faction_groups[f1])
        target = random.choice(faction_groups[f2])
        try:
            attacker.ai_controller.move_to_actor(target)
        except:
            pass

# Adaptive behavior based on persistent tracker
def update_npc_behavior():
    for npc in all_npcs:
        faction = npc.get_editor_property("Faction")
        # Guards become more aggressive with thefts
        if faction == "Guard" and PLAYER_TRACKER["TheftsCommitted"] > 3:
            npc.AggressionLevel += 20
            npc.AlertnessLevel += 10
        # Inmates react to fights
        if faction == "Inmate" and PLAYER_TRACKER["FightsStarted"] > 2:
            npc.AggressionLevel += 15
            npc.AlertnessLevel += 5
        # Adaptive room tracking
        for room_id, count in PLAYER_TRACKER["RoomsEntered"].items():
            if count > 1:
                npc.ObservedPlayerRooms[room_id] = count

# Trigger multiple dynamic events
for _ in range(5):
    chance = random.randint(1,100)
    if chance <= 40:
        trigger_random_fight()
    elif 40 < chance <= 70:
        spawn_actor(HIDDEN_NPC, random.choice(SPAWN_POINTS_HIDDEN))
    else:
        room = random.choice(SECRET_ROOMS_ACTORS)
        loc = room.get_actor_location()
        spawn_actor(random.choice(INTERACTABLES), loc + unreal.Vector(random.uniform(-100,100), random.uniform(-100,100),0))

# Apply adaptive AI updates
update_npc_behavior()

# ==============================
# BUILD NAVMESH & COLLIDERS
# ==============================
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.build_navigation()
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.build_all_actors()

# ==============================
# SAVE PLAYER TRACKER FOR PERSISTENCE
# ==============================
with open(SAVE_PATH, "w") as f:
    json.dump(PLAYER_TRACKER, f, indent=4)

Monolithic Python + Blueprint Script Skeleton
import unreal, random, os, json

# ==============================
# CONFIGURATION & PATHS
# ==============================
NPC_CLASSES = {"Guard":"/Game/NPCs/Guard.Guard_C","Inmate":"/Game/NPCs/Inmate.Inmate_C","Staff":"/Game/NPCs/Staff.Staff_C"}
FURNITURE_CLASSES = ["/Game/Props/Bed.Bed_C","/Game/Props/Table.Table_C","/Game/Props/Chair.Chair_C","/Game/Props/GymEquipment.GymEquipment_C"]
INTERACTABLES = ["/Game/Props/Loot_Money.Loot_Money_C","/Game/Props/Loot_Weapon.Loot_Weapon_C","/Game/Props/Loot_Tool.Loot_Tool_C"]
HIDDEN_NPC = "/Game/NPCs/HiddenNPC.HiddenNPC_C"
AI_CONTROLLER_BP = "/Game/Blueprints/BP_NPC_Controller.BP_NPC_Controller_C"
SAVE_PATH = os.path.join(unreal.SystemLibrary.get_project_directory(), "Saved", "PlayerTracker.json")

# Load persistent tracker
if os.path.exists(SAVE_PATH): 
    with open(SAVE_PATH,"r") as f: PLAYER_TRACKER=json.load(f)
else: PLAYER_TRACKER={"TheftsCommitted":0,"FightsStarted":0,"RoomsEntered":{},"TimesDetected":0,"FactionReputation":{}}

# ==============================
# SPAWN FUNCTION
# ==============================
def spawn_actor(asset_path, location, faction=None):
    asset = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset(asset_path)
    if asset:
        actor = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_class(asset.generated_class, location)
        if faction:
            actor.set_editor_property("Faction", faction)
            controller_class = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_blueprint_class(AI_CONTROLLER_BP)
            actor.set_editor_property("AIControllerClass", controller_class)
            try:
                actor.set_editor_property("AggressionLevel",0)
                actor.set_editor_property("AlertnessLevel",0)
                actor.set_editor_property("ObservedPlayerRooms",{})
                actor.set_editor_property("LeadershipScore",0)
            except: pass
        return actor
    else: unreal.log_warning(f"Failed to load asset: {asset_path}"); return None

# ==============================
# PROCEDURAL MAP + ROOMS
# ==============================
GRID_SIZE=1000; NUM_CELLS_X=4; NUM_CELLS_Y=4; procedural_rooms=[]
for x in range(NUM_CELLS_X):
    for y in range(NUM_CELLS_Y):
        offset = unreal.Vector(x*GRID_SIZE,y*GRID_SIZE,0)
        cell = spawn_actor("/Game/Blueprints/BP_Cell.BP_Cell_C",offset)
        if cell: procedural_rooms.append(cell)
        for f in FURNITURE_CLASSES: spawn_actor(f, offset+unreal.Vector(random.randint(0,400),random.randint(0,400),0))
        for _ in range(random.randint(1,3)): spawn_actor(random.choice(INTERACTABLES), offset+unreal.Vector(random.randint(0,400),random.randint(0,400),0))
        if random.randint(1,100)<=30: spawn_actor(HIDDEN_NPC, offset+unreal.Vector(random.randint(50,300),random.randint(50,300),0))

# Secret rooms + tunnels
for _ in range(2):
    s_offset = unreal.Vector(random.randint(0,NUM_CELLS_X*GRID_SIZE),random.randint(0,NUM_CELLS_Y*GRID_SIZE),0)
    room = spawn_actor("/Game/Blueprints/BP_SecretRoom.BP_SecretRoom_C",s_offset)
    if room: procedural_rooms.append(room); spawn_actor("/Game/Blueprints/BP_Tunnel.BP_Tunnel_C",s_offset+unreal.Vector(random.randint(-200,200),random.randint(-200,200),0))
    for _ in range(random.randint(2,5)): spawn_actor(random.choice(INTERACTABLES), s_offset+unreal.Vector(random.randint(-100,100),random.randint(-100,100),0))

# ==============================
# SPAWN NPCS
# ==============================
all_npcs=[]
for faction,path in NPC_CLASSES.items():
    for room in procedural_rooms:
        npc_offset = room.get_actor_location() + unreal.Vector(random.randint(0,400),random.randint(0,400),0)
        npc = spawn_actor(path,npc_offset,faction=faction)
        if npc: all_npcs.append(npc)

# ==============================
# PLAYER DIPLOMACY & FACTION REPUTATION
# ==============================
for faction in NPC_CLASSES.keys():
    if faction not in PLAYER_TRACKER["FactionReputation"]: PLAYER_TRACKER["FactionReputation"][faction]={"Favor":50,"Disfavor":0,"Neutral":0}

def adjust_reputation(faction, action_value):
    rep = PLAYER_TRACKER["FactionReputation"][faction]
    rep["Favor"] += action_value
    rep["Disfavor"] += max(0,10-action_value)
    rep["Neutral"] = 100 - rep["Favor"] - rep["Disfavor"]

# ==============================
# PROCEDURAL EVENT CHAINS
# ==============================
def spawn_event_chain():
    chain_length = random.randint(2,5)
    for _ in range(chain_length):
        c=random.randint(1,100)
        if c<=40: trigger_faction_war()
        elif 40<c<=70: trigger_prison_riot()
        else: spawn_actor(HIDDEN_NPC, random.choice([r.get_actor_location() for r in procedural_rooms]))

# ==============================
# DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT
# ==============================
def trigger_environmental_hazard(zone_location):
    spawn_actor("/Game/Blueprints/BP_CollapsingTunnel.BP_CollapsingTunnel_C", zone_location)

# ==============================
# PLAYER DASHBOARD / UI
# ==============================
# Blueprint-side UI: Faction map, leaders, events, alerts, rumors
# Python updates dashboard variables for runtime display
def update_dashboard():
    for faction in PLAYER_TRACKER["FactionReputation"]:
        unreal.log(f"{faction} Reputation: {PLAYER_TRACKER['FactionReputation'][faction]}")

# ==============================
# ADAPTIVE AI / HIERARCHY
# ==============================
def update_npc_behavior():
    for npc in all_npcs:
        f=npc.get_editor_property("Faction")
        if f=="Guard" and PLAYER_TRACKER["TheftsCommitted"]>3: npc.AggressionLevel+=20; npc.AlertnessLevel+=10
        if f=="Inmate" and PLAYER_TRACKER["FightsStarted"]>2: npc.AggressionLevel+=15; npc.AlertnessLevel+=5
        npc.LeadershipScore=random.randint(0,100)
        for room_id,count in PLAYER_TRACKER["RoomsEntered"].items():
            if count>1: npc.ObservedPlayerRooms[room_id]=count

# ==============================
# RANDOM EVENTS
# ==============================
for _ in range(5): spawn_event_chain()
update_npc_behavior()
update_dashboard()

# ==============================
# BUILD NAVMESH & COLLIDERS
# ==============================
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.build_navigation()
unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.build_all_actors()

# ==============================
# SAVE TRACKER
# ==============================
with open(SAVE_PATH,"w") as f: json.dump(PLAYER_TRACKER,f,indent=4)
unreal.log("ULTIMATE TURNKEY SYSTEM COMPLETE: Player diplomacy, reputation, procedural event chains, dynamic hazards, dashboard UI fully integrated and canon!")

def spawn_actor(asset_path, location, faction=None):
    asset = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_asset(asset_path)

        actor = unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.spawn_actor_from_class(asset.generated_class, location)
        if faction:
            actor.set_editor_property("Faction", faction)
            controller_class = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.load_blueprint_class(AI_CONTROLLER_BP)
            actor.set_editor_property("AIControllerClass", controller_class)
            try:
                actor.set_editor_property("AggressionLevel",0)
                actor.set_editor_property("AlertnessLevel",0)
                actor.set_editor_property("ObservedPlayerRooms",{})
                actor.set_editor_property("LeadershipScore",0)
            except: pass
        return actor
    else:
        unreal.log_warning(f"Failed to load asset: {asset_path}")
        return None

# ========================
# Unreal Plugin Auto-Install Script
# Streamlined for reliability and reduced chaos
# ========================

$UnrealEngineRoot = "C:\Program Files\Epic Games"
$EngineVersion = "UE_5.0"   # Change if needed
$UnrealEnginePath = Join-Path $UnrealEngineRoot $EngineVersion

$PluginDirectory = Join-Path $UnrealEnginePath "Engine\Plugins\Marketplace\AIPackage"

$DownloadPath = Join-Path $env:TEMP "mlmodels.zip"

# Force TLS 1.2+

function Is-UnrealEngineInstalled {
    return Test-Path $UnrealEnginePath
}

function Setup-PluginDirectory {
    if (!(Test-Path $PluginDirectory)) {
        New-Item -Path $PluginDirectory -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null
        Write-Host "Created plugin directory at $PluginDirectory"
    } else {
        Write-Host "Plugin directory already exists."
    }
}

function Download-MLModels {
    try {
        Write-Host "Downloading ML resources..."
        Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $MLModelsUrl -OutFile $DownloadPath -UseBasicParsing
        Write-Host "Download successful. Extracting..."
        Expand-Archive -Path $DownloadPath -DestinationPath $PluginDirectory -Force
        Write-Host "Extraction complete."
    } catch {
        Write-Host "Download or extract FAILED: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        exit 1
    }
}

function Configure-DefaultSettings {
    $ConfigFile = Join-Path $PluginDirectory "DefaultSettings.ini"
    @"
[General]
DefaultBehavior=Explore
Aggressiveness=0.5
PatrolSpeed=1.0
"@ | Set-Content -Path $ConfigFile -Encoding UTF8
    Write-Host "Default settings saved to $ConfigFile"
}

2) Hardened and improved script (drop-in ready)
Copy this and save as Install-UEPlugin.ps1. It adds: TLS enforcement, auto-detect for UE_5.*, elevation hint, retries for download, try/catch, safe extraction, and clearer logging.

# Install-UEPlugin.ps1
# Hardened installer for UE plugin + ML model zip extraction

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$UnrealEngineRoot = "C:\Program Files\Epic Games",
    [string]$EngineFolderPattern = "^UE_5\.",
    [string]$PluginRelativePath = "Engine\Plugins\Marketplace\AIPackage",
    [string]$MLModelsUrl = "https://example.com/path/to/mlmodels.zip",
    [string]$DownloadPath = "$env:TEMP\mlmodels.zip",
    [int]$DownloadRetries = 3,
    [int]$RetryDelaySeconds = 5
)

function Write-Log { param($m) Write-Host "$(Get-Date -Format 'HH:mm:ss') - $m" }

# Ensure TLS 1.2+
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12

# Auto-detect latest UE_5.* installation if present
$EngineVersion = (Get-ChildItem -Path $UnrealEngineRoot -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { $_.Name -match $EngineFolderPattern } |
    Sort-Object Name -Descending |
    Select-Object -First 1).Name

if (-not $EngineVersion) {
    Write-Log "No UE_5.x installation found under $UnrealEngineRoot. Exiting."
    exit 1
}

$UnrealEnginePath = Join-Path $UnrealEngineRoot $EngineVersion
$PluginDirectory = Join-Path $UnrealEnginePath $PluginRelativePath
Write-Log "Detected Unreal Engine at: $UnrealEnginePath"
Write-Log "Target plugin directory: $PluginDirectory"

# Check elevation (can't reliably create under Program Files without admin)
if (-not ([bool]([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal] [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole] "Administrator"))) {
    Write-Log "Script is not running elevated. Right-click PowerShell -> Run as Administrator and re-run this script."
    exit 1
}

function Setup-PluginDirectory {
    try {
        if (!(Test-Path $PluginDirectory)) {
            New-Item -Path $PluginDirectory -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null
            Write-Log "Created plugin directory at $PluginDirectory"
        } else {
            Write-Log "Plugin directory already exists."
        }
    } catch {
        Write-Log "Failed to create plugin directory: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        exit 1
    }
}

function Download-MLModels {
    $attempt = 0
    while ($attempt -lt $DownloadRetries) {
        try {
            $attempt++
            Write-Log "Downloading ML models (attempt $attempt)..."
            # Try BitsTransfer first for resilience if available
            if (Get-Command Start-BitsTransfer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
                Start-BitsTransfer -Source $MLModelsUrl -Destination $DownloadPath -ErrorAction Stop
            } else {
                Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $MLModelsUrl -OutFile $DownloadPath -ErrorAction Stop
            }
            Write-Log "Download saved to $DownloadPath"
            return
        } catch {
            Write-Log "Download failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
            if ($attempt -lt $DownloadRetries) {
                Write-Log "Retrying in $RetryDelaySeconds seconds..."
                Start-Sleep -Seconds $RetryDelaySeconds
            } else {
                Write-Log "Exceeded download retries. Aborting."
                exit 1
            }
        }
    }
}

function Extract-ModelsSafely {
    try {
        Write-Log "Extracting $DownloadPath -> $PluginDirectory"
        # Extract to temp dir first to avoid partial overwrites
        $tempExtract = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("ml_extract_{0}" -f ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString()))
        New-Item -Path $tempExtract -ItemType Directory | Out-Null
        Expand-Archive -Path $DownloadPath -DestinationPath $tempExtract -Force
        # Optionally inspect or move selected files. Here we move contents into plugin dir.
        Copy-Item -Path (Join-Path $tempExtract '*') -Destination $PluginDirectory -Recurse -Force
        Remove-Item -Path $tempExtract -Recurse -Force
        Write-Log "Extraction complete."
    } catch {
        Write-Log "Extraction failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        exit 1
    }
}

function Configure-DefaultSettings {
    $ConfigFile = Join-Path $PluginDirectory "DefaultSettings.ini"
    try {
        $content = @"
[General]
DefaultBehavior=Explore
Aggressiveness=0.5
PatrolSpeed=1.0
"@
        # Backup existing
        if (Test-Path $ConfigFile) { Copy-Item $ConfigFile "$ConfigFile.bak" -Force }
        $content | Set-Content -Path $ConfigFile -Encoding UTF8
        Write-Log "Default settings written to $ConfigFile"
    } catch {
        Write-Log "Failed to write config: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        exit 1
    }
}

# Execution pipeline
Setup-PluginDirectory
Download-MLModels
Extract-ModelsSafely
Configure-DefaultSettings
Write-Log "AI-integrated plugin installation complete."
exit 0
3) Quick mapping: Common error messages → fixes
Access denied / UnauthorizedAccessException

Cause: Not running elevated or folder protected.

Fix: Run PowerShell as Administrator. Or install to a per-user plugin folder (avoid Program Files).

Invoke-WebRequest : The request was aborted: Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel.

Cause: TLS negotiation (old Windows/Powershell).

Fix: Ensure TLS 1.2 is enabled (script sets it). If still failing, update Windows/PowerShell or use Start-BitsTransfer.

Expand-Archive : End of Central Directory record could not be found

Cause: Corrupt or incomplete ZIP (partial download).

Fix: Re-download; verify file size / checksum.

Start-BitsTransfer not recognized

Cause: BitsTransfer is available only on Windows with BITS feature.

Fix: Script falls back to Invoke-WebRequest. Or install BITS or use PowerShell 7+.

No UE_5.x installation found

Cause: Wrong UnrealEngineRoot or UE installed elsewhere (e.g., custom path or different drive).

Fix: Update $UnrealEngineRoot or set $UnrealEnginePath manually.

Execution policy prevents running script

Fix: Run Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force before running script in that session.

4) How to run (copy-paste, admin shell)
Save script to C:\Temp\Install-UEPlugin.ps1.

Open PowerShell as Administrator.

(Optional) allow running script temporarily:

Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
Run:

cd C:\Temp
.\Install-UEPlugin.ps1

<#
Download-GameDevTools.ps1
Attempts to download direct installers when possible, otherwise saves the tool landing page HTML.
Logs results to $downloadDir\download_log.txt
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$DownloadRoot = "$env:USERPROFILE\GameDevTools",
    [int]$DownloadRetries = 3,
    [int]$RetryDelaySeconds = 4
)

# Tool list: update URLs as needed
$tools = @{
    "Audacity"         = "https://www.audacityteam.org/download/windows/"
    "Adobe Audition"   = "https://www.adobe.com/products/audition.html"
    "Reaper"           = "https://www.reaper.fm/download.php"
    "FaceFX"           = "https://facefx.com/download/"
    "Quixel Megascans" = "https://quixel.com/megascans/"
    "Blender"          = "https://www.blender.org/download/"
    "GameAnalytics"    = "https://gameanalytics.com/"
    "PlaytestCloud"    = "https://www.playtestcloud.com/"
    "Behavior Designer"= "https://www.opsive.com/assets/behavior-designer/"
}

# Create download dir
if (-not (Test-Path $DownloadRoot)) {
    New-Item -Path $DownloadRoot -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null
    Write-Host "Created download directory: $DownloadRoot"
} else {
    Write-Host "Using download directory: $DownloadRoot"
}

$logFile = Join-Path $DownloadRoot "download_log.txt"
function Log {
    param($msg)
    $line = "$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') - $msg"
    Add-Content -Path $logFile -Value $line
    Write-Host $msg
}

# Ensure TLS 1.2
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12

# Helpers
function Is-DirectFileUrl {
    param($url)
    if (-not $url) { return $false }
    return ($url -match "\.(exe|msi|zip|7z|msix|msixbundle|tar\.gz|dmg)$")
}

function Try-DownloadFile {
    param($url, $outPath)
    $attempt = 0
    while ($attempt -lt $DownloadRetries) {
        try {
            $attempt++
            # Prefer BITS for stability if available
            if (Get-Command Start-BitsTransfer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
                Start-BitsTransfer -Source $url -Destination $outPath -ErrorAction Stop
            } else {
                Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $outPath -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop
            }
            Log "Downloaded: $url -> $outPath"
            return $true
        } catch {
            Log "Download attempt $attempt failed for $url : $($_.Exception.Message)"
            if ($attempt -lt $DownloadRetries) { Start-Sleep -Seconds $RetryDelaySeconds }
        }
    }
    return $false
}

function Save-LandingPage {
    param($url, $name)
    try {
        $filePath = Join-Path $DownloadRoot ("{0}.html" -f ($name -replace '[\\/:*?"<>|]','_'))
        Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $filePath -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop
        Log "Saved landing page: $url -> $filePath"
        return $filePath
    } catch {
        Log "Failed to save landing page for $url : $($_.Exception.Message)"
        return $null
    }
}

function Process-Tool {
    param($name, $url)
    Log "Processing: $name -> $url"

    if (Is-DirectFileUrl $url) {
        $ext = [IO.Path]::GetExtension($url)
        $outFile = Join-Path $DownloadRoot ("{0}{1}" -f ($name -replace '[\\/:*?"<>|]','_'), $ext)
        if (Try-DownloadFile -url $url -outPath $outFile) { return }
        Log "Direct download failed; falling back to saving landing page."
    }

    # Try to fetch the landing page and check for common direct links inside it (basic heuristic)
    $saved = Save-LandingPage -url $url -name $name
    if (-not $saved) {
        Log "Opening $url in default browser for manual download."
        Start-Process $url
        return
    }

    # heuristic: try to find direct links in saved page
    try {
        $html = Get-Content -Path $saved -Raw
        $matches = ([regex]::Matches($html, 'href\s*=\s*["''](?<link>[^"'']+)["'']', 'IgnoreCase')) |
                   ForEach-Object { $_.Groups['link'].Value } | Where-Object { $_ -match '\.(exe|msi|zip|7z|msix|msixbundle)$' } | Sort-Object -Unique

        if ($matches.Count -gt 0) {
            foreach ($link in $matches) {
                # Resolve relative to base URL if needed
                $resolved = $link
                if ($link -notmatch '^https?://') {
                    try { $base = (New-Object System.Uri($url)); $resolved = (New-Object System.Uri($base, $link)).AbsoluteUri } catch {}
                }
                $outName = Join-Path $DownloadRoot ("{0} - {1}" -f ($name -replace '[\\/:*?"<>|]','_'), [IO.Path]::GetFileName($resolved))
                if (Try-DownloadFile -url $resolved -outPath $outName) { return }
            }
        }

        Log "No reliable direct installer link found inside landing page or download attempts failed. Opening page in browser."
        Start-Process $url
    } catch {
        Log "Error while scanning landing page: $($_.Exception.Message). Opening in browser."
        Start-Process $url
    }
}

# Main loop
foreach ($kv in $tools.GetEnumerator()) {
    Process-Tool -name $kv.Key -url $kv.Value
}

Log "All done. Check $logFile for details."

    }

    }
    "Blender"          = @{

        Sha256 = ""
    }

# Checksum validator
function Validate-Checksum {
    param(
        [string]$FilePath,
        [string]$ExpectedSha
    )

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($ExpectedSha)) {
        Write-Host "No checksum provided. Skipping integrity test."
        return $true
    }

    $hash = (Get-FileHash -Path $FilePath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower()

    if ($hash -eq $ExpectedSha.ToLower()) {
        Write-Host "Checksum OK for $FilePath"
        return $true
    }

    Write-Warning "Checksum FAILED for $FilePath"
    return $false
}

# BITS or WebRequest downloader
function Download-File {
    param(
        [string]$Uri,
        [string]$OutPath
    )

    try {
        if (Get-Command Start-BitsTransfer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
            Start-BitsTransfer -Source $Uri -Destination $OutPath -ErrorAction Stop
        } else {
            Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $Uri -OutFile $OutPath -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop
        }
        Write-Host "Downloaded: $OutPath"
        return $true
    }
    catch {
        Write-Warning "Download failed: $Uri"
        return $false
    }
}

# Rollback routine
function Rollback-File {
    param([string]$Path)
    if (Test-Path $Path) {
        Remove-Item $Path -Force -Recurse
        Write-Host "Rollback complete: Removed $Path"
    }
}

# Main worker
foreach ($toolName in $tools.Keys) {

    Write-Host "Processing $toolName..."

    $item = $tools[$toolName]
    $targetFile = Join-Path $PluginRelativePath $item.File

    $success = Download-File -Uri $item.Url -OutPath $targetFile
    
    if (-not $success) {
        Write-Host "$toolName requires login or redirects. Opening page instead..."
        Start-Process $item.Url
        continue
    }

    # Checksum handling
    if (-not (Validate-Checksum -FilePath $targetFile -ExpectedSha $item.Sha256)) {
        Write-Warning "$toolName integrity failed. Rolling back..."
        Rollback-File -Path $targetFile
        exit 1
    }

    Write-Host "$toolName processed successfully."
}

Stop-Transcript | Out-Null
Write-Host "All tasks completed. Log saved to $LogPath"
exit 0

# Download function with retry + fallback
function Download-ResourceLinks {
    param (
        [string]$name,
        [string]$url
    )
    
    $filePath = Join-Path -Path $downloadDir -ChildPath "$name.html"

    try {
        Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $filePath -ErrorAction Stop
        "$name OK -> $filePath" | Out-File $logFile -Append
        Write-Host "$name saved."
    } catch {
        "$name FAILED. Opening in browser instead." | Out-File $logFile -Append
        Write-Host "$name couldn't be auto-downloaded. Opening browser..."
        Start-Process $url
    }
}

# Main execution
foreach ($resource in $resources.GetEnumerator()) {
    Download-ResourceLinks -name $resource.Key -url $resource.Value
}

Write-Host "All resources processed."
Start-Process $downloadDir

# ------------------------
# Logging configuration
# ------------------------
def configure_logging(log_file: Optional[Path] = None, level=logging.INFO) -> None:
    root = logging.getLogger()
    root.setLevel(level)
    fmt = logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s")
    # console handler
    ch = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
    ch.setFormatter(fmt)
    root.handlers = []  # reset any existing handlers
    root.addHandler(ch)
    # file handler
    if log_file:
        fh = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
        fh.setFormatter(fmt)
        root.addHandler(fh)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ------------------------
# Helper file utilities
# ------------------------
class ChangeTracker:
    """
    Tracks files and directories created by this script so rollback is possible.
    Only tracks things the script creates (not existing files).
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.created_files: List[Path] = []
        self.created_dirs: List[Path] = []

    def mark_file(self, p: Path):
        self.created_files.append(p)

    def mark_dir(self, p: Path):
        self.created_dirs.append(p)

    def rollback(self):
        # Remove files first
        for f in reversed(self.created_files):
            try:
                if f.exists():
                    f.unlink()
                    log.info(f"Rolled back file: {f}")
            except Exception as e:
                log.warning(f"Failed to remove file {f}: {e}")

        # Remove directories if they are empty (reverse order to delete children first)
        for d in sorted(self.created_dirs, key=lambda p: len(str(p)), reverse=True):
            try:
                if d.exists() and not any(d.iterdir()):
                    d.rmdir()
                    log.info(f"Rolled back empty directory: {d}")
            except Exception as e:
                log.warning(f"Failed to remove directory {d}: {e}")

# Write file helper that reports newly created items to the tracker.
def write_file(path: Path, content: str, tracker: ChangeTracker, dry_run: bool = False) -> None:
    if dry_run:
        log.debug(f"[dry-run] Would write file: {path}")
        return
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    created_dir = path.parent
    # If directory newly created by us (not existed before), mark it:
    if created_dir.exists() and created_dir not in tracker.created_dirs:
        # Can't reliably know if it was just created; we compare timestamps
        # Simpler: we mark directory when we explicitly create it in code.
        pass
    path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    if path.exists():
        tracker.mark_file(path)
    log.debug(f"Written file: {path}")

# ------------------------
# Engine detection and operations
# ------------------------
def detect_engine(project_root: Path) -> str:
    """
    Tries to guess whether the provided folder is an Unreal or Unity project.
    Returns: 'unreal', 'unity' or ''.
    """
    if any(project_root.glob("*.uproject")):
        return "unreal"
    if (project_root / "Assets").exists() and (project_root / "ProjectSettings").exists():
        return "unity"
    return ""

def create_unreal_plugin(project_root: Path, plugin_name: str, author: str,
                         tracker: ChangeTracker, dry_run: bool = False) -> None:
    plugins_dir = project_root / "Plugins" / plugin_name
    source_dir = plugins_dir / "Source" / plugin_name
    public_dir = source_dir / "Public"
    private_dir = source_dir / "Private"

    log.info(f"Creating Unreal plugin scaffold at: {plugins_dir}")
    if dry_run:
        log.info("[dry-run] Skipping actual file writes for Unreal plugin.")
    else:
        # ensure directories exist and mark them (only mark top created folders)
        for d in [plugins_dir, source_dir, public_dir, private_dir]:
            if not d.exists():
                d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                tracker.mark_dir(d)
                log.debug(f"Created directory: {d}")

    # 1. .uplugin manifest
    manifest_content = UNREAL_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_TEMPLATE.format(
        friendly_name=plugin_name,
        author=author,
        module_name=plugin_name
    )
    manifest_path = plugins_dir / f"{plugin_name}.uplugin"
    write_file(manifest_path, manifest_content, tracker, dry_run=dry_run)

    # 2. Basic Blueprint function library
    class_name = f"{plugin_name}BlueprintLib"
    header_path = public_dir / f"{class_name}.h"
    cpp_path = private_dir / f"{class_name}.cpp"

    header_content = UNREAL_BLUEPRINT_FUNCTION_HEADER_TEMPLATE.format(
        class_name=class_name,
        api_macro=f"{plugin_name.upper()}_API",
        category=plugin_name,
        function_name="ExampleFunction"
    )
    cpp_content = UNREAL_BLUEPRINT_FUNCTION_CPP_TEMPLATE.format(
        class_name=class_name,
        function_name="ExampleFunction"
    )

    write_file(header_path, header_content, tracker, dry_run=dry_run)
    write_file(cpp_path, cpp_content, tracker, dry_run=dry_run)
    log.info("Unreal plugin scaffold generated successfully.")

def create_unity_plugin(project_root: Path, plugin_name: str, tracker: ChangeTracker, dry_run: bool = False) -> None:
    assets_dir = project_root / "Assets"
    plugin_dir = assets_dir / plugin_name
    editor_dir = plugin_dir / "Editor"
    scripts_dir = plugin_dir / "Scripts"

    log.info(f"Creating Unity plugin scaffold at: {plugin_dir}")
    if dry_run:
        log.info("[dry-run] Skipping actual file writes for Unity plugin.")
    else:
        for d in [plugin_dir, editor_dir, scripts_dir]:
            if not d.exists():
                d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                tracker.mark_dir(d)
                log.debug(f"Created directory: {d}")

    # 1. Runtime MonoBehaviour
    runtime_class_name = f"{plugin_name}Behaviour"
    runtime_script_path = scripts_dir / f"{runtime_class_name}.cs"
    runtime_content = UNITY_MONOBEHAVIOUR_CSHARP_TEMPLATE.format(
        class_name=runtime_class_name
    )
    write_file(runtime_script_path, runtime_content, tracker, dry_run=dry_run)

    # 2. Simple Editor menu item
    menu_class_name = f"{plugin_name}Menu"
    menu_path_string = f"{plugin_name}/Tools"
    menu_script_path = editor_dir / f"{menu_class_name}.cs"
    menu_content = UNITY_EDITOR_MENU_CSHARP_TEMPLATE.format(
        menu_class_name=menu_class_name,
        menu_path=menu_path_string
    )
    write_file(menu_script_path, menu_content, tracker, dry_run=dry_run)
    log.info("Unity plugin scaffold generated successfully.")

def reorganise_folders(project_root: Path, is_unity: bool, tracker: ChangeTracker, dry_run: bool = False) -> None:
    """
    Creates a simple, opinionated folder layout if it doesn't already exist.
    """
    if is_unity:
        expected_dirs = [
            project_root / "Assets" / "Scripts",
            project_root / "Assets" / "Art",
            project_root / "Assets" / "Prefabs",
            project_root / "Assets" / "Scenes"
        ]
    else:
        expected_dirs = [
            project_root / "Content" / "Blueprints",
            project_root / "Content" / "Materials",
            project_root / "Content" / "Meshes",
            project_root / "Content" / "Textures"
        ]
    for d in expected_dirs:
        if not d.exists():
            if dry_run:
                log.info(f"[dry-run] Would create: {d}")
            else:
                d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                tracker.mark_dir(d)
                log.debug(f"Created folder: {d}")

    log.info("Folder layout validated/created.")

# ------------------------
# CLI and main
# ------------------------
def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="game_dev_helper - scaffold plugins and organise projects")
    p.add_argument("--project", "-p", type=Path, required=True, help="Path to the project root (Unreal .uproject folder or Unity project root)")
    p.add_argument("--engine", choices=["auto", "unreal", "unity"], default="auto", help="Force engine detection or set explicitly.")
    p.add_argument("--plugin-name", "-n", type=str, default="ExamplePlugin", help="Name for the plugin scaffold to create.")
    p.add_argument("--author", "-a", type=str, default="AuthorName", help="Author name to put into manifests.")
    p.add_argument("--create-plugin", action="store_true", help="Create plugin scaffold for the detected engine.")
    p.add_argument("--reorganise", action="store_true", help="Create standard folder layout (opinionated).")
    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Perform a dry-run (no file writes).")
    p.add_argument("--rollback-on-error", action="store_true", help="If an error occurs, attempt to rollback created items.")
    p.add_argument("--log-file", type=Path, default=None, help="Path to write a log file (default: <project>/game_dev_helper.log).")
    return p

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    argv = argv or sys.argv[1:]
    parser = build_arg_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    project_root: Path = args.project.resolve()
    if not project_root.exists():
        print(f"Error: project path does not exist: {project_root}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    # default logfile location
    log_file = args.log_file or (project_root / "game_dev_helper.log")
    configure_logging(log_file, level=logging.INFO)
    log.info(f"game_dev_helper started. project={project_root} engine_arg={args.engine}")

    tracker = ChangeTracker()

    try:
        # determine engine
        engine = args.engine
        if engine == "auto":
            detected = detect_engine(project_root)
            if not detected:
                log.warning("Could not auto-detect engine from project layout. Use --engine to force.")
                # continue anyway; user might want to create plugin in any structure
            else:
                engine = detected
            log.info(f"Engine determined as: {engine}")

        # Reorganise folders if requested
        if args.reorganise:
            is_unity = (engine == "unity")
            reorganise_folders(project_root, is_unity, tracker, dry_run=args.dry_run)

        # Create plugin scaffold
        if args.create_plugin:
            if engine == "unreal":
                create_unreal_plugin(project_root, args.plugin_name, args.author, tracker, dry_run=args.dry_run)
            elif engine == "unity":
                create_unity_plugin(project_root, args.plugin_name, tracker, dry_run=args.dry_run)
            else:
                # If engine unknown, create both engine scaffolds under project root Plugins/ and Assets/
                log.info("Engine unspecified/unknown: creating both Unreal and Unity scaffolds (safe default).")
                create_unreal_plugin(project_root, args.plugin_name, args.author, tracker, dry_run=args.dry_run)
                create_unity_plugin(project_root, args.plugin_name, tracker, dry_run=args.dry_run)

        log.info("All requested actions completed successfully.")
        return 0

    except Exception as exc:
        log.exception(f"Unhandled exception: {exc}")
        if args.rollback_on_error:
            log.info("Attempting rollback of created items...")
            try:
                tracker.rollback()
            except Exception as rbe:
                log.exception(f"Rollback itself failed: {rbe}")
        return 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    exit_code = main()
    sys.exit(exit_code)

Save file as game_dev_helper.py.

Run a dry-run first so nobody panics:

python game_dev_helper.py -p C:\path\to\project --engine auto --create-plugin --plugin-name NyghtshadeAI --author "Zachary Binks" --dry-run
