Want to reorganize folders too:

python game_dev_helper.py -p C:\path\to\project --reorganise --create-plugin --rollback-on-error
Check <project>/game_dev_helper.log for a full audit trail.

Notes, caveats, and guilt-free improvements
The rollback system removes files the script created and empty directories if they are empty. It will not delete non-empty directories to avoid accidental data loss. If you want a harsher rollback, I can add a forced mode that nukes entire plugin directories, but that’s a dangerous power move.

Header/cpp/cs templates are minimal. I intentionally avoid inserting complex macros or engine-version-specific scaffolding so this stays broadly useful.

If you want the plugin to include build scripts, module .Build.cs for Unreal, AssemblyDefinition for Unity, or README and license files — say so. I’ll add them.

If you want this as a proper PowerShell or Rust CLI later, I’ll happily spit that out too. You said “Yes” earlier; let’s keep momentum.

• Clean JSON: No BOM, no comments, no stray commas. UE’s parser is petty and fragile.

Quick checklist so things don’t explode:
Define the CSS variables in your global CSS (or <html> / :root) and provide dark-mode overrides using .dark. Example:

:root {
  --background: 210 16% 98%;
  --foreground: 220 15% 8%;
  --font-sans: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif;
  /* ...etc... */
}
.dark {
  --background: 222 20% 7%;
  --foreground: 210 20% 95%;
}
Install the plugins: npm i -D tailwindcss-animate @tailwindcss/typography

If you want strict types and IDE help, keep satisfies Config — that’s gold.

If any color still looks off, check the actual HSL composition stored in your CSS variables — Tailwind is faithfully rendering what you tell it, not what your brain imagines.

Deployment Types

Static Deployments
Deployment Types
Static Deployments
Static Deployments publish your static websites and frontend apps to a cost-effective cloud server.

Copy page

Static Deployments host your Replit App’s static files, such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript on a cloud server. The server automatically uses caching and scaling strategies to deliver your content quickly and economically.
Static Deployments are ideal for the following use cases:
		Marketing landing pages
		Portfolio websites
		Product and API documentation sites

Static Deployments are not compatible with Replit Apps created using Agent. Agent automatically creates full-stack apps that require a backend server. For Agent-generated apps, use one of the following deployment types: - Autoscale Deployment - Reserved VM Deployment

 


​

Features
Static Deployments include the following features:
		Cost-effective hosting: Pay only for the amount of data your website serves.
		HTTP routing options: Configure response headers, URL rewrites, and redirects.
		Custom domains: Configure a custom domain or use a <app-name>.replit.app URL to access your app.
		Custom error pages: Create and serve a custom 404 error page.
		Monitoring: View logs and monitor your published app’s status.
​

Usage
You can access Static Deployments in the Deployments workspace tool.


How to access Static Deployments

 


​

Primary domain
Specify the subdomain part of the hostname for your published app. After you publish, you can access your published app at https://<subdomain>.replit.app.
To learn how to use a custom domain, see Custom Domains.
​

Private deployment

The private published app feature is available for Teams and Enterprise plans only.
Private published apps grant permission to your app only to members of your team or organization. This control lets you toggle whether to make your published app private.
To learn how to set up a private deployment, see Private Deployments.
​

Public directory
Specify the base directory path in your Replit App that contains the static files you want to serve publicly. After you deploy, the cloud host serves all pages and assets in that directory.
The default value, /, is the root directory of your Replit App.
​

Build command
Specify a build command to run in your Replit App’s shell when you create your Deployment.
For example, if you generate a static site using Hugo, you might use the command hugo --minify to generate the files and optimize asset file sizes.
​

Deployment secrets
Select Add deployment secret to add environment variables or secrets your build command needs to run securely.
For example, if your site generator requires an API key to create your static site, you might pass it API_KEY=<your secret name>.
​

		Usage Allowances: Learn about scheduled deployment usage limits and billing units

# =============================================================================
# File: game_builder_ai.py
# Description:
#     High-level utility that helps automate workflow steps shared between
#     Unreal Engine 5 and Unity.  It handles folder management, basic “mod”
#     injection, Blueprint / Behaviour Tree scaffolding, and delegates heavy
#     lifting to each engine’s own Python integration layer (Unreal’s built-in
#     Python interpreter and Unity’s “Python for Unity” package).
#
#     IMPORTANT:
#         • This file is intentionally lightweight; it does NOT expose or wrap
#           the full editor APIs.  Instead, it illustrates one coherent, fully
#           runnable pattern you can extend inside each engine.
#         • Actual generation of complex game content still requires engine
#           tooling (e.g. editor scripting, C++ modules, C# assemblies, etc.).
#         • Keep this script in a location reachable by both editors or install
#           it as a pip-installable package in your Python environment.
#
# Author:  Your Name
# License: MIT
# =============================================================================

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
# Global logging setup
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s  [%(levelname)s]  %(name)s ›  %(message)s",
    handlers=[logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)],
)
logger = logging.getLogger("GameBuilderAI")


# =============================================================================
# Configuration manager
# =============================================================================
class ConfigManager:
    """
    Simple JSON-backed settings helper.
    """

    def __init__(self, cfgPath: Path):
        self.cfgPath: Path = cfgPath.expanduser().resolve()
        self.data: Dict = {}
        if self.cfgPath.exists():
            self.load()
        else:
            self._createDefaultFile()

    # .........................................................................
    def _createDefaultFile(self) -> None:
        self.data = {
            "unreal": {"projectRoot": "", "pluginsFolder": "Plugins"},
            "unity": {"projectRoot": "", "packagesFolder": "Packages"},
            "ai": {"provider": "stub", "apiKey": ""},
        }
        self.save()
        logger.info("Created default config at %s", self.cfgPath)

    # .........................................................................
    def load(self) -> None:
        self.data = json.loads(self.cfgPath.read_text())
        logger.debug("Loaded configuration from %s", self.cfgPath)

    # .........................................................................
    def save(self) -> None:
        self.cfgPath.write_text(json.dumps(self.data, indent=4))
        logger.debug("Saved configuration to %s", self.cfgPath)

    # .........................................................................
    def get(self, path: str, fallback: Optional[str] = None):
        """
        Retrieve nested configuration value using dotted path notation.
        """
        keys = path.split(".")
        node = self.data
        for key in keys:
            if key not in node:
                return fallback
            node = node[key]
        return node

    # .........................................................................
    def set(self, path: str, value):
        keys = path.split(".")
        node = self.data
        for key in keys[:-1]:
            node = node.setdefault(key, {})
        node[keys[-1]] = value
        logger.debug("Config updated: %s → %s", path, value)
        self.save()


# =============================================================================
# Folder helper
# =============================================================================
class FolderManager:
    """
    Convenience wrappers around file-system operations common during modding
    (copying content, cleaning build folders, etc.).
    """

    def __init__(self, dryRun: bool = False):
        self.dryRun = dryRun

    # .........................................................................
    def copyRecursive(self, src: Path, dst: Path, ignorePatterns: Optional[List[str]] = None):
        logger.info("Copying %s → %s", src, dst)
        if self.dryRun:
            return
        ignore = shutil.ignore_patterns(*(ignorePatterns or []))
        shutil.copytree(src, dst, dirs_exist_ok=True, ignore=ignore)

    # .........................................................................
    def ensureFolder(self, path: Path):
        if not path.exists():
            logger.debug("Creating folder %s", path)
            if not self.dryRun:
                path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


# =============================================================================
# Engine-specific helpers
# =============================================================================
class UnrealManager:
    """
    Minimal Unreal Engine 5 automation hooks.
    Requires: Unreal Editor with Python enabled.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: ConfigManager):
        self.projectRoot = Path(config.get("unreal.projectRoot", ""))

    # .........................................................................
    def runEditorCommand(self, pythonCode: str):
        """
        Spawns Unreal Editor (headless) and executes a Python one-liner.
        Adjust 'UE4Editor' path depending on your installation.
        """
        editorExe = Path(os.environ.get("UE_EDITOR", "UnrealEditor"))
        cmd = [
            str(editorExe),
            str(self.projectRoot / f"{self.projectRoot.stem}.uproject"),
            "-run=pythonscript",
            f"-script={pythonCode}",
            "-unattended",
            "-nopause",
        ]
        logger.info("Running Unreal command: %s", " ".join(cmd))
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

    # .........................................................................
    def generateBlueprint(self, name: str, outputDir: Path):
        template = f"""
import unreal

package = unreal.load_package("{outputDir.as_posix()}")
blueprintFactory = unreal.BlueprintFactory()
assetTools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()
assetTools.create_asset("{name}", "{outputDir.as_posix()}", None, blueprintFactory)
"""
        self.runEditorCommand(template)
        logger.info("Blueprint '%s' generation request dispatched.", name)


class UnityManager:
    """
    Minimal Unity automation hooks (tested with 'Python for Unity' package).
    """

    def __init__(self, config: ConfigManager):
        self.projectRoot = Path(config.get("unity.projectRoot", ""))

    # .........................................................................
    def runEditorCommand(self, pythonFile: Path, args: Optional[List[str]] = None):
        """
        Calls Unity in batch-mode, executing a python file through the package.
        """
        unityExe = Path(os.environ.get("UNITY_EDITOR", "Unity"))
        cmd = [
            str(unityExe),
            "-projectPath", str(self.projectRoot),
            "-batchmode",
            "-quit",
            "-executeMethod", "PythonRunner.RunFile",
            "-file", str(pythonFile.resolve()),
        ]
        if args:
            cmd.extend(args)
        logger.info("Running Unity command: %s", " ".join(cmd))
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

    # .........................................................................
    def scaffoldBehaviour(self, name: str, outputDir: Path):
        pyScript = outputDir / f"create_{name}.py"
        pyScript.write_text(
            f"""
import UnityEditor
import UnityEngine as ue

assetPath = "Assets/{name}.asset"
tree = ue.BehaviorTree()
ue.AssetDatabase.CreateAsset(tree, assetPath)
"""
        )
        self.runEditorCommand(pyScript)
        logger.info("Behaviour Tree '%s' scaffold request dispatched.", name)

# AI planner (placeholder stub)
# =============================================================================
class AIPlanner:
    """
    Decides which assets should be generated next.
    Replace this stub with calls to your preferred ML/LLM provider.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: ConfigManager):
        self.config = config

    # .........................................................................
    def proposeNextTask(self, userPrompt: str) -> Dict:
        logger.info("AIPlanner analyzing prompt: %s", userPrompt)
        # Placeholder: always suggest a generic blueprint/behaviour pair
        return {
            "blueprint": {"name": "BP_AutoGenerated", "folder": "Content/AutoGen"},
            "behaviour": {"name": "BT_AutoGenerated", "folder": "Assets/AutoGen"},
        }


# =============================================================================
# Main CLI
# =============================================================================
def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="GameBuilderAI",
        description="Assistant utility for Unreal Engine 5 and Unity projects.",
    )

    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    initCmd = sub.add_parser("init", help="Create default configuration file.")
    initCmd.add_argument("--path", default="~/.game_builder_ai.json")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    planCmd = sub.add_parser("plan", help="Generate next asset plan via AI.")
    planCmd.add_argument("prompt", help="Free-form text describing the goal.")
    planCmd.add_argument("--cfg", default="~/.game_builder_ai.json")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    execCmd = sub.add_parser("exec", help="Execute previously generated plan.")
    execCmd.add_argument(
        "planFile", help="JSON file produced by the 'plan' command."
    )
    execCmd.add_argument("--dry", action="store_true", help="Dry-run filesystem ops.")
    execCmd.add_argument("--cfg", default="~/.game_builder_ai.json")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    if args.command == "init":
        cfg = ConfigManager(Path(args.path))
        logger.info("Config ready at %s", cfg.cfgPath)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    elif args.command == "plan":
        cfg = ConfigManager(Path(args.cfg))
        planner = AIPlanner(cfg)
        plan = planner.proposeNextTask(args.prompt)
        outFile = Path.cwd() / "ai_build_plan.json"
        outFile.write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=4))
        logger.info("Plan saved to %s", outFile)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    elif args.command == "exec":
        cfg = ConfigManager(Path(args.cfg))
        planPath = Path(args.planFile).resolve()
        plan = json.loads(planPath.read_text())
        folderMgr = FolderManager(dryRun=args.dry)

        # Unreal part
        unrealMgr = UnrealManager(cfg)
        bpInfo = plan.get("blueprint")
        if bpInfo:
            uFolder = Path(cfg.get("unreal.projectRoot")) / bpInfo["folder"]
            folderMgr.ensureFolder(uFolder)
            unrealMgr.generateBlueprint(bpInfo["name"], uFolder)

        # Unity part
        unityMgr = UnityManager(cfg)
        btInfo = plan.get("behaviour")
        if btInfo:
            uFolder = Path(cfg.get("unity.projectRoot")) / btInfo["folder"]
            folderMgr.ensureFolder(uFolder)
            unityMgr.scaffoldBehaviour(btInfo["name"], uFolder)

        logger.info("Execution complete.")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# File: game_builder_ai.py
# Updated, hardened version for safer editor automation
# Author: Generated for ZACHARY BINKS (edit author as needed)
# License: MIT

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Logging
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s  [%(levelname)s]  %(name)s ›  %(message)s",
    handlers=[logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)],
)
logger = logging.getLogger("GameBuilderAI")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ConfigManager (safe defaults + path resolution)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
class ConfigManager:
    def __init__(self, cfgPath: Path):
        self.cfgPath = cfgPath.expanduser().resolve()
        self.data: Dict = {}
        if self.cfgPath.exists():
            try:
                self.load()
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error("Failed to parse config %s: %s", self.cfgPath, e)
                raise
        else:
            self._createDefaultFile()

    def _createDefaultFile(self) -> None:
        self.data = {
            "unreal": {"projectRoot": "", "pluginsFolder": "Plugins"},
            "unity": {"projectRoot": "", "packagesFolder": "Packages"},
            "ai": {"provider": "stub", "apiKey": ""},
        }
        self.save()
        logger.info("Created default config at %s", self.cfgPath)

    def load(self) -> None:
        raw = self.cfgPath.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.data = json.loads(raw)
        logger.debug("Loaded configuration from %s", self.cfgPath)

    def save(self) -> None:
        self.cfgPath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.cfgPath.write_text(json.dumps(self.data, indent=4), encoding="utf-8")
        logger.debug("Saved configuration to %s", self.cfgPath)

    def get(self, path: str, fallback: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
        keys = path.split(".")
        node = self.data
        for key in keys:
            if isinstance(node, dict) and key in node:
                node = node[key]
            else:
                return fallback
        return node

    def set(self, path: str, value) -> None:
        keys = path.split(".")
        node = self.data
        for key in keys[:-1]:
            node = node.setdefault(key, {})
        node[keys[-1]] = value
        logger.debug("Config updated: %s → %s", path, value)
        self.save()


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simple folder helper
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
class FolderManager:
    def __init__(self, dryRun: bool = False):
        self.dryRun = dryRun

    def copyRecursive(self, src: Path, dst: Path, ignorePatterns: Optional[List[str]] = None):
        logger.info("Copying %s → %s", src, dst)
        if self.dryRun:
            logger.debug("[dry-run] Skipping copyRecursive")
            return
        ignore = shutil.ignore_patterns(*(ignorePatterns or []))
        shutil.copytree(src, dst, dirs_exist_ok=True, ignore=ignore)

    def ensureFolder(self, path: Path):
        logger.debug("Ensuring folder exists: %s", path)
        if self.dryRun:
            logger.debug("[dry-run] Would create folder: %s", path)
            return
        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Utility helpers
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def find_executable(names: List[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Try to find an executable by name using environment var fallback and PATH lookup.
    Returns full path or None.
    """
    for name in names:
        # check env var first (common pattern: UE_EDITOR, UNITY_EDITOR)
        env_path = os.environ.get(name.upper())
        if env_path:
            if shutil.which(env_path) or Path(env_path).exists():
                return env_path
        # try plain name via PATH
        exe = shutil.which(name)
        if exe:
            return exe
    return None


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unreal manager
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
class UnrealManager:
    def __init__(self, config: ConfigManager, dryRun: bool = False):
        self.projectRoot = Path(config.get("unreal.projectRoot", "") or "").expanduser()
        self.pluginsFolder = config.get("unreal.pluginsFolder", "Plugins")
        self.dryRun = dryRun

    def _resolve_editor(self) -> Optional[str]:
        # Check common env var names then common executable names
        candidates = ["UE_EDITOR", "UnrealEditor", "UnrealEditor.exe", "UE4Editor", "UE5Editor"]
        exe = find_executable(candidates)
        if exe:
            logger.debug("Found Unreal editor at: %s", exe)
        else:
            logger.warning("Unreal editor not found in PATH or UE_EDITOR env var.")
        return exe

    def runEditorCommandFile(self, pythonFile: Path) -> None:
        """
        Prefer running a python file via the editor. This writes a temporary script and asks the editor
        to execute it. The exact CLI flags may depend on engine version and packaging.
        """
        if not self.projectRoot or not (self.projectRoot.exists()):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Unreal projectRoot not configured or does not exist: {self.projectRoot}")

        editorExe = self._resolve_editor()
        if not editorExe:
            raise FileNotFoundError("Unreal editor executable not found. Set UE_EDITOR env var or install in PATH.")

        # Example invocation: UnrealEditor <uproject> -run=pythonscript -script="C:/path/script.py" -unattended -nopause
        uproject = self.projectRoot / f"{self.projectRoot.stem}.uproject"
        if not uproject.exists():
            logger.warning("Unreal .uproject file not found: %s (editor may still accept project root)", uproject)

        cmd = [
            str(editorExe),
            str(uproject),
            "-run=pythonscript",
            f"-script={str(pythonFile)}",
            "-unattended",
            "-nopause",
        ]
        logger.info("Running Unreal Editor command: %s", " ".join(cmd))
        if self.dryRun:
            logger.info("[dry-run] Would run: %s", " ".join(cmd))
            return

        try:
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
            logger.error("Unreal Editor command failed: %s", e)
            raise

    def generateBlueprint(self, name: str, outputDir: Path) -> None:
        """
        Generate a simple blueprint asset using Unreal's Python API by writing a small script
        and invoking the editor. This is intentionally minimal and must be adapted to your
        engine version and API availability.
        """
        outputDir = outputDir.resolve()
        logger.info("Requesting blueprint generation: %s -> %s", name, outputDir)
        # create folder if needed
        if not self.dryRun:
            outputDir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # Create a temporary python file with Unreal Python API calls
        script_content = f"""
import unreal
# Note: This script will run inside the editor's python environment.
package_path = "/Game/{outputDir.name}"
asset_name = "{name}"
# Minimal: create an empty blueprint (requires a proper factory/module in a real pipeline)
ue_log = unreal.log
ue_log("Creating asset: {{}} at {{}}".format(asset_name, package_path))
# advanced steps would be here: use BlueprintFactory, AssetToolsHelpers, etc.
"""
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".py", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as tmp:
            tmp.write(script_content)
            tmp_path = Path(tmp.name)
        logger.debug("Wrote temp Unreal script to %s", tmp_path)

        try:
            self.runEditorCommandFile(tmp_path)
        finally:
            try:
                if tmp_path.exists():
                    tmp_path.unlink()
                    logger.debug("Removed temp script %s", tmp_path)
            except Exception:
                logger.debug("Failed to remove temp script %s", tmp_path)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unity manager
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
class UnityManager:
    def __init__(self, config: ConfigManager, dryRun: bool = False):
        self.projectRoot = Path(config.get("unity.projectRoot", "") or "").expanduser()
        self.dryRun = dryRun

    def _resolve_editor(self) -> Optional[str]:
        candidates = ["UNITY_EDITOR", "Unity", "Unity.exe"]
        exe = find_executable(candidates)
        if exe:
            logger.debug("Found Unity editor at: %s", exe)
        else:
            logger.warning("Unity editor not found in PATH or UNITY_EDITOR env var.")
        return exe

    def runEditorCommand(self, pythonFile: Path, args: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> None:
        if not self.projectRoot or not (self.projectRoot.exists()):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Unity projectRoot not configured or does not exist: {self.projectRoot}")

        editorExe = self._resolve_editor()
        if not editorExe:
            raise FileNotFoundError("Unity editor executable not found. Set UNITY_EDITOR env var or install in PATH.")

        cmd = [
            str(editorExe),
            "-projectPath", str(self.projectRoot),
            "-batchmode",
            "-quit",
            "-executeMethod", "PythonRunner.RunFile",
            "-file", str(pythonFile.resolve()),
        ]
        if args:
            cmd.extend(args)

        logger.info("Running Unity Editor command: %s", " ".join(cmd))
        if self.dryRun:
            logger.info("[dry-run] Would run: %s", " ".join(cmd))
            return

        try:
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
            logger.error("Unity Editor command failed: %s", e)
            raise

    def scaffoldBehaviour(self, name: str, outputDir: Path) -> None:
        outputDir = outputDir.resolve()
        logger.info("Requesting behaviour scaffold: %s -> %s", name, outputDir)
        if not self.dryRun:
            outputDir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # create a python file expected by "Python for Unity" package
        script_text = f'''# Auto-generated by GameBuilderAI - runs inside Unity's Python for Unity package
from UnityEditor import AssetDatabase
from UnityEngine import Debug

# Minimal placeholder: actual Behavior Tree classes require a package (third-party)
Debug.Log("Scaffold placeholder for behavior: {name}")
# In a real pipeline you'd create the asset with API calls here.
'''
        tmp = None
        try:
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".py", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as tmpf:
                tmpf.write(script_text)
                tmp = Path(tmpf.name)
            logger.debug("Wrote temp Unity script to %s", tmp)
            self.runEditorCommand(tmp)
        finally:
            if tmp and tmp.exists():
                try:
                    tmp.unlink()
                    logger.debug("Removed temp Unity script: %s", tmp)
                except Exception:
                    logger.debug("Failed to remove temp Unity script: %s", tmp)

Additional advice (read this before you run editors)
Run with --dry first. It will create temp scripts and show you what it would do. Don’t be that person who launches the editor full of half-formed Python and wonders why everything exploded.

Set unreal.projectRoot and unity.projectRoot in the config created by init. Example:

{
  "unreal": {"projectRoot": "C:/Projects/MyUEProject", "pluginsFolder":"Plugins"},
  "unity": {"projectRoot": "C:/Projects/MyUnityProject", "packagesFolder":"Packages"},
  "ai": {"provider":"stub","apiKey":""}
}
Editor CLI flags vary by engine and by version. The template used here is generic. If your Unreal/Unity install requires different flags, adjust the runEditorCommandFile and runEditorCommand methods.

Security: never run untrusted AI output directly through an editor. LLMs can hallucinate API calls; always inspect generated scripts.

CI usage: Make sure the CI runner actually has headless editors installed and licensed. Headless editor invocation in CI often needs licensing / special flags.

# =============================================================================
# Configuration manager
# =============================================================================
class ConfigManager:
    """
    Simple JSON-backed settings helper.
    """

    def __init__(self, cfgPath: Path):
        self.cfgPath: Path = cfgPath.expanduser().resolve()
        self.data: Dict = {}
        if self.cfgPath.exists():
            self.load()
        else:
            self._createDefaultFile()

    # .........................................................................
    def _createDefaultFile(self) -> None:
        self.data = {
            "unreal": {"projectRoot": "", "pluginsFolder": "Plugins"},
            "unity": {"projectRoot": "", "packagesFolder": "Packages"},
            "ai": {"provider": "stub", "apiKey": ""},
        }
        self.save()
        logger.info("Created default config at %s", self.cfgPath)

    # .........................................................................
    def load(self) -> None:
        self.data = json.loads(self.cfgPath.read_text())
        logger.debug("Loaded configuration from %s", self.cfgPath)

    # .........................................................................
    def save(self) -> None:
        self.cfgPath.write_text(json.dumps(self.data, indent=4))
        logger.debug("Saved configuration to %s", self.cfgPath)

    # .........................................................................
    def get(self, path: str, fallback: Optional[str] = None):
        """
        Retrieve nested configuration value using dotted path notation.
        """
        keys = path.split(".")
        node = self.data
        for key in keys:
            if key not in node:
                return fallback
            node = node[key]
        return node

    # .........................................................................
    def set(self, path: str, value):
        keys = path.split(".")
        node = self.data
        for key in keys[:-1]:
            node = node.setdefault(key, {})
        node[keys[-1]] = value
        logger.debug("Config updated: %s → %s", path, value)
        self.save()


# =============================================================================
# Folder helper
# =============================================================================
class FolderManager:
    """
    Convenience wrappers around file-system operations common during modding
    (copying content, cleaning build folders, etc.).
    """

    def __init__(self, dryRun: bool = False):
        self.dryRun = dryRun

    # .........................................................................
    def copyRecursive(self, src: Path, dst: Path, ignorePatterns: Optional[List[str]] = None):
        logger.info("Copying %s → %s", src, dst)
        if self.dryRun:
            return
        ignore = shutil.ignore_patterns(*(ignorePatterns or []))
        shutil.copytree(src, dst, dirs_exist_ok=True, ignore=ignore)

    # .........................................................................
    def ensureFolder(self, path: Path):
        if not path.exists():
            logger.debug("Creating folder %s", path)
            if not self.dryRun:
                path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# game_builder_ai.py — safer, hardened version (drop-in replacement)
# Author: Generated for ZACHARY BINKS

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

# Logging

# --------------------------
# Config manager
# --------------------------
class ConfigManager:
    def __init__(self, cfg_path: Path):
        self.cfg_path = cfg_path.expanduser().resolve()
        self.data: Dict = {}
        if self.cfg_path.exists():
            self.load()
        else:
            self._create_default()

    def _create_default(self) -> None:
        self.data = {
            "unreal": {"projectRoot": "", "pluginsFolder": "Plugins"},
            "unity": {"projectRoot": "", "packagesFolder": "Packages"},
            "ai": {"provider": "stub", "apiKey": ""},
        }
        self.save()
        logger.info("Created default config at %s", self.cfg_path)

    def load(self) -> None:
        raw = self.cfg_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.data = json.loads(raw)
        logger.debug("Loaded config from %s", self.cfg_path)

    def save(self) -> None:
        self.cfg_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.cfg_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.data, indent=4), encoding="utf-8")
        logger.debug("Saved config to %s", self.cfg_path)

    def get(self, dotted: str, fallback: Optional[str] = None):
        node = self.data
        for key in dotted.split("."):
            if not isinstance(node, dict) or key not in node:
                return fallback
            node = node[key]
        return node

    def set(self, dotted: str, value) -> None:
        node = self.data
        keys = dotted.split(".")
        for k in keys[:-1]:
            node = node.setdefault(k, {})
        node[keys[-1]] = value
        self.save()

# --------------------------
# FS helper
# --------------------------
class FolderManager:
    def __init__(self, dry_run: bool = False):
        self.dry_run = dry_run

    def ensure(self, path: Path):
        logger.debug("Ensure folder: %s", path)
        if self.dry_run:
            logger.info("[dry-run] would create folder %s", path)
            return
        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# --------------------------
# Utilities
# --------------------------
def find_executable(env_names: List[str], fallback_names: List[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    # check env vars first
    for n in env_names:
        val = os.environ.get(n)
        if val and (Path(val).exists() or shutil.which(val)):
            return val
    # then PATH by name
    for n in fallback_names:
        p = shutil.which(n)
        if p:
            return p
    return None

# --------------------------
# Unreal manager
# --------------------------
class UnrealManager:
    def __init__(self, cfg: ConfigManager, dry_run: bool = False):
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.project_root = Path(cfg.get("unreal.projectRoot", "") or "").expanduser()
        self.dry_run = dry_run

    def _resolve_editor(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return find_executable(["UE_EDITOR"], ["UnrealEditor", "UnrealEditor.exe", "UE4Editor", "UE5Editor"])

    def run_python_script(self, script_text: str):
        editor = self._resolve_editor()
        if not editor:
            raise FileNotFoundError("Unreal editor not found (set UE_EDITOR or put editor in PATH)")

        # write script to a temp file
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".py", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as tf:
            tf.write(script_text)
            tmp_path = Path(tf.name)

        uproject = self.project_root / f"{self.project_root.stem}.uproject"
        cmd = [str(editor), str(uproject), "-run=pythonscript", f"-script={str(tmp_path)}", "-unattended", "-nopause"]
        logger.info("Running Unreal command: %s", " ".join(cmd))
        if self.dry_run:
            logger.info("[dry-run] would run Unreal with temp script %s", tmp_path)
            tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            return

        try:
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
        finally:
            tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def generate_blueprint(self, name: str, out_folder: Path):
        logger.info("Requesting blueprint generation: %s -> %s", name, out_folder)
        out_folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        script = f"""import unreal
unreal.log("Creating blueprint {name} in /Game/{out_folder.name}")
# NOTE: Implement robust asset creation via BlueprintFactory + AssetToolsHelpers here as needed.
"""
        self.run_python_script(script)

    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    init = sub.add_parser("init", help="Create default config")
    init.add_argument("--path", default="~/.game_builder_ai.json")
    plan = sub.add_parser("plan", help="Generate a plan (AI stub)")
    plan.add_argument("prompt")
    plan.add_argument("--out", default="ai_build_plan.json")
    execp = sub.add_parser("exec", help="Execute a plan")
    execp.add_argument("planfile")
    execp.add_argument("--dry", action="store_true", help="Dry run (no editor spawn)")
    return p

def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    argv = argv or sys.argv[1:]
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    cfg_path = Path(args.cfg).expanduser().resolve()

    if args.cmd == "init":
        cfg = ConfigManager(Path(args.path).expanduser().resolve())
        logger.info("Config created at %s", cfg.cfg_path)
        return 0

    cfg = ConfigManager(cfg_path)

    if args.cmd == "plan":
        planner = AIPlanner(cfg)
        plan = planner.propose(args.prompt)
        outp = Path(args.out).resolve()
        outp.write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=4), encoding="utf-8")
        logger.info("Plan written to %s", outp)
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "exec":
        planpath = Path(args.planfile).expanduser().resolve()
        if not planpath.exists():
            logger.error("Plan file not found: %s", planpath)
            return 2
        plan = json.loads(planpath.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        fm = FolderManager(dry_run=args.dry)

        # Unreal
        try:
            um = UnrealManager(cfg, dry_run=args.dry)
            bp = plan.get("blueprint")
            if bp:
                out = Path(cfg.get("unreal.projectRoot", "") or "") / bp.get("folder", "AutoGen")
                fm.ensure(out)
                um.generate_blueprint(bp.get("name", "BP_AutoGenerated"), out)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Unreal execution failed: %s", e)
            return 1

        # Unity
        try:
            xm = UnityManager(cfg, dry_run=args.dry)
            bt = plan.get("behaviour")
            if bt:
                out = Path(cfg.get("unity.projectRoot", "") or "") / bt.get("folder", "AutoGen")
                fm.ensure(out)
                xm.scaffold_behaviour(bt.get("name", "BT_AutoGenerated"), out)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Unity execution failed: %s", e)
            return 1

        logger.info("Execution finished successfully.")
        return 0

    return 2

if __name__ == "__main__":
    rc = main()
    sys.exit(rc)

# =============================================================================
# File: game_builder_ai.py
# Description:
#     High-level utility that helps automate workflow steps shared between
#     Unreal Engine 5 and Unity. It handles folder management, basic "mod"
#     injection, Blueprint / Behaviour Tree scaffolding, and delegates heavy
#     lifting to each engine's own Python integration layer.
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   - Lightweight: does NOT wrap full editor APIs. Extend inside engine scripts.
#   - Requires editors installed and (optionally) env vars UE_EDITOR / UNITY_EDITOR.
# Author: Your Name
# License: MIT
# =============================================================================

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s  [%(levelname)s]  %(name)s ›  %(message)s",
    handlers=[logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)],
)
logger = logging.getLogger("GameBuilderAI")


# =============================================================================
# Configuration manager
# =============================================================================
class ConfigManager:
    """
    Simple JSON-backed settings helper.
    """

    def __init__(self, cfgPath: Path):
        self.cfgPath: Path = cfgPath.expanduser().resolve()
        self.data: Dict = {}
        if self.cfgPath.exists():
            self.load()
        else:
            self._createDefaultFile()

    def _createDefaultFile(self) -> None:
        self.data = {
            "unreal": {"projectRoot": "", "pluginsFolder": "Plugins"},
            "unity": {"projectRoot": "", "packagesFolder": "Packages"},
            "ai": {"provider": "stub", "apiKey": ""},
        }
        self.save()
        logger.info("Created default config at %s", self.cfgPath)

    def load(self) -> None:
        raw = self.cfgPath.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.data = json.loads(raw)
        logger.debug("Loaded configuration from %s", self.cfgPath)

    def save(self) -> None:
        self.cfgPath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.cfgPath.write_text(json.dumps(self.data, indent=4), encoding="utf-8")
        logger.debug("Saved configuration to %s", self.cfgPath)

    def get(self, path: str, fallback: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Retrieve nested configuration value using dotted path notation.
        """
        keys = path.split(".")
        node = self.data
        for key in keys:
            if not isinstance(node, dict) or key not in node:
                return fallback
            node = node[key]
        return node

    def set(self, path: str, value) -> None:
        keys = path.split(".")
        node = self.data
        for key in keys[:-1]:
            node = node.setdefault(key, {})
        node[keys[-1]] = value
        logger.debug("Config updated: %s → %s", path, value)
        self.save()


# =============================================================================
# Folder helper
# =============================================================================
class FolderManager:
    """
    Convenience wrappers around file-system operations common during modding.
    """

    def __init__(self, dryRun: bool = False):
        self.dryRun = dryRun

    def copyRecursive(self, src: Path, dst: Path, ignorePatterns: Optional[List[str]] = None):
        logger.info("Copying %s → %s", src, dst)
        if self.dryRun:
            logger.debug("[dry-run] copy skipped")
            return
        ignore = shutil.ignore_patterns(*(ignorePatterns or []))
        shutil.copytree(src, dst, dirs_exist_ok=True, ignore=ignore)

    def ensureFolder(self, path: Path):
        if not path.exists():
            logger.debug("Creating folder %s", path)
            if not self.dryRun:
                path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


# =============================================================================
# Engine-specific helpers
# =============================================================================
def find_executable(env_names: List[str], fallbacks: List[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    # check env vars first
    for env in env_names:
        p = os.environ.get(env)
        if p and (Path(p).exists() or shutil.which(p)):
            return p
    # then PATH fallbacks
    for name in fallbacks:
        exe = shutil.which(name)
        if exe:
            return exe
    return None


class UnrealManager:
    """
    Minimal Unreal Engine 5 automation hooks.
    Requires: Unreal Editor with Python enabled.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: ConfigManager, dryRun: bool = False):
        self.projectRoot = Path(config.get("unreal.projectRoot", "") or "").expanduser()
        self.dryRun = dryRun

    def _resolve_editor(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return find_executable(["UE_EDITOR"], ["UnrealEditor", "UnrealEditor.exe", "UE5Editor", "UE4Editor"])

    def runEditorCommandFile(self, pythonFile: Path) -> None:
        editorExe = self._resolve_editor()
        if not editorExe:
            raise FileNotFoundError("Unreal editor not found. Set UE_EDITOR or put editor in PATH.")
        uproject = self.projectRoot / f"{self.projectRoot.stem}.uproject"
        cmd = [
            str(editorExe),
            str(uproject),
            "-run=pythonscript",
            f"-script={str(pythonFile)}",
            "-unattended",
            "-nopause",
        ]
        logger.info("Running Unreal command: %s", " ".join(cmd))
        if self.dryRun:
            logger.info("[dry-run] would run Unreal command")
            return
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

    def generateBlueprint(self, name: str, outputDir: Path):
        outputDir = outputDir.resolve()
        logger.info("Requesting blueprint generation: %s -> %s", name, outputDir)
        if not self.dryRun:
            outputDir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        script = f"""
import unreal
unreal.log("Creating blueprint {name} in /Game/{outputDir.name}")
# Real pipeline should use AssetToolsHelpers + BlueprintFactory to create assets
"""
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".py", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as tmp:
            tmp.write(script)
            tmp_path = Path(tmp.name)
        try:
            self.runEditorCommandFile(tmp_path)
        finally:
            try:
                if tmp_path.exists():
                    tmp_path.unlink()
            except Exception:
                logger.debug("Temp file cleanup failed: %s", tmp_path)


class UnityManager:
    """
    Minimal Unity automation hooks (tested with 'Python for Unity' package).
    """

    def __init__(self, config: ConfigManager, dryRun: bool = False):
        self.projectRoot = Path(config.get("unity.projectRoot", "") or "").expanduser()
        self.dryRun = dryRun

    def _resolve_editor(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return find_executable(["UNITY_EDITOR"], ["Unity", "Unity.exe"])

    def runEditorCommand(self, pythonFile: Path, args: Optional[List[str]] = None):
        unityExe = self._resolve_editor()
        if not unityExe:
            raise FileNotFoundError("Unity editor not found. Set UNITY_EDITOR or put Unity in PATH.")
        cmd = [
            str(unityExe),
            "-projectPath", str(self.projectRoot),
            "-batchmode",
            "-quit",
            "-executeMethod", "PythonRunner.RunFile",
            "-file", str(pythonFile.resolve()),
        ]
        if args:
            cmd.extend(args)
        logger.info("Running Unity command: %s", " ".join(cmd))
        if self.dryRun:
            logger.info("[dry-run] would run Unity command")
            return
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

    def scaffoldBehaviour(self, name: str, outputDir: Path):
        outputDir = outputDir.resolve()
        logger.info("Requesting behaviour scaffold: %s -> %s", name, outputDir)
        if not self.dryRun:
            outputDir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        pyScript = outputDir / f"create_{name}.py"
        content = (
            "import UnityEditor\n"
            "import UnityEngine as ue\n\n"
            f'ue.Debug.Log("Scaffold placeholder for behavior: {name}")\n'
            "# Replace with real Behavior Tree creation calls when running inside Unity.\n"
        )
        if self.dryRun:
            logger.debug("[dry-run] would write Unity script at %s", pyScript)
        else:
            pyScript.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
        self.runEditorCommand(pyScript)

def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="GameBuilderAI",
        description="Assistant utility for Unreal Engine 5 and Unity projects.",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    initCmd = sub.add_parser("init", help="Create default configuration file.")
    initCmd.add_argument("--path", default="~/.game_builder_ai.json")

    planCmd = sub.add_parser("plan", help="Generate next asset plan via AI.")
    planCmd.add_argument("prompt", help="Free-form text describing the goal.")
    planCmd.add_argument("--cfg", default="~/.game_builder_ai.json")

    execCmd = sub.add_parser("exec", help="Execute previously generated plan.")
    execCmd.add_argument("planFile", help="JSON file produced by the 'plan' command.")
    execCmd.add_argument("--dry", action="store_true", help="Dry-run filesystem ops.")
    execCmd.add_argument("--cfg", default="~/.game_builder_ai.json")

    return parser


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    argv = argv or sys.argv[1:]
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.command == "init":
        cfg = ConfigManager(Path(args.path).expanduser().resolve())
        logger.info("Config ready at %s", cfg.cfgPath)
        return 0

    if args.command == "plan":
        cfg = ConfigManager(Path(args.cfg))
        planner = AIPlanner(cfg)
        plan = planner.proposeNextTask(args.prompt)
        outFile = Path.cwd() / "ai_build_plan.json"
        outFile.write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=4), encoding="utf-8")
        logger.info("Plan saved to %s", outFile)
        return 0

    if args.command == "exec":
        cfg = ConfigManager(Path(args.cfg))
        planPath = Path(args.planFile).resolve()
        if not planPath.exists():
            logger.error("Plan file not found: %s", planPath)
            return 2
        plan = json.loads(planPath.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        folderMgr = FolderManager(dryRun=args.dry)

        # Unreal part
        unrealMgr = UnrealManager(cfg, dryRun=args.dry)
        bpInfo = plan.get("blueprint")
        if bpInfo:
            uRoot = Path(cfg.get("unreal.projectRoot", "") or "")
            uFolder = (uRoot / bpInfo["folder"]).expanduser().resolve()
            folderMgr.ensureFolder(uFolder)
            try:
                unrealMgr.generateBlueprint(bpInfo["name"], uFolder)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.exception("Unreal generation failed: %s", e)
                return 1

        # Unity part
        unityMgr = UnityManager(cfg, dryRun=args.dry)
        btInfo = plan.get("behaviour")
        if btInfo:
            jRoot = Path(cfg.get("unity.projectRoot", "") or "")
            uFolder = (jRoot / btInfo["folder"]).expanduser().resolve()
            folderMgr.ensureFolder(uFolder)
            try:
                unityMgr.scaffoldBehaviour(btInfo["name"], uFolder)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.exception("Unity scaffold failed: %s", e)
                return 1

        logger.info("Execution complete.")
        return 0

    return 2


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    rc = main()
    sys.exit(rc)
How to use (quick):

Save as game_builder_ai.py.

Initialize config:
python game_builder_ai.py init --path ~/.game_builder_ai.json
Edit that JSON and set unreal.projectRoot and unity.projectRoot.

Generate a plan (stubbed AI):
python game_builder_ai.py plan "create AI guard behavior" --cfg ~/.game_builder_ai.json

Inspect ai_build_plan.json, then run in dry mode:
python game_builder_ai.py exec ai_build_plan.json --dry --cfg ~/.game_builder_ai.json

If dry-run looks good, run without --dry.

ChatGPT said:
Let’s wire the stubbed AI into a safe LLM adapter with prompt templates and a verification step. That way, your plan command actually generates meaningful, guided asset plans instead of the placeholder blueprint/behaviour pair, and we can add a verification step to make sure the AI isn’t proposing nonsense that could break your project.

Here’s the approach I’d take:

1️⃣ LLM Adapter Class
import openai  # or any LLM SDK you prefer

class SafeLLMAdapter:
    """
    Wraps LLM calls safely, using prompt templates and a verification step.
    """
    def __init__(self, api_key: str):
        self.api_key = api_key
        openai.api_key = self.api_key

    def generate_plan(self, user_prompt: str) -> dict:
        template = f"""
        You are a game dev assistant. 
        Given the goal: "{user_prompt}", propose:
        1. A blueprint name and folder for Unreal.
        2. A behaviour tree name and folder for Unity.
        Return as strict JSON: {{
            "blueprint": {{"name": "<string>", "folder": "<string>"}},
            "behaviour": {{"name": "<string>", "folder": "<string>"}}
        }}
        Ensure folder paths are valid subpaths under project roots.
        """

        response = openai.ChatCompletion.create(
            model="gpt-4",
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": template}],
            temperature=0.3
        )

        try:
            plan_json = response.choices[0].message.content
            plan = json.loads(plan_json)
            # Verification step
            assert "blueprint" in plan and "behaviour" in plan
            return plan
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error("LLM output invalid: %s", e)
            return {
                "blueprint": {"name": "BP_Fallback", "folder": "Content/AutoGen"},
                "behaviour": {"name": "BT_Fallback", "folder": "Assets/AutoGen"},
            }
2️⃣ Hook it into AIPlanner
class AIPlanner:
    def __init__(self, config: ConfigManager):
        self.config = config
        self.adapter = SafeLLMAdapter(config.get("ai.apiKey"))

    def proposeNextTask(self, userPrompt: str) -> dict:
        logger.info("AIPlanner analyzing prompt: %s", userPrompt)
        return self.adapter.generate_plan(userPrompt)

Safe AI-driven planning with fallback.

Keeps your existing plan and exec workflow unchanged.

Manual trigger & release logic
